picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for Virginia Tech vs. Pitt - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus 49ers owner suspended, fined WNBA playoffs CBS, Tony Romo part ways Browns outlast Steelers Duren, Pistons reach deal Three Bold Predictions for Virginia Tech vs. Pitt Sep 19, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; Virginia Tech Hokies quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer (17) waits for a timeout to end in the first half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect James Duncan Fri, October 2, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Pitt hasn't allowed a point in the first or third quarter this season. Pitt also hasn't left Pittsburgh. That changes today at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN, when the Panthers (4-0, 1-0 ACC) walk into a sold-out Lane Stadium to face a Virginia Tech team (4-0, 1-0 ACC) chasing its first 5-0 start since 2005. The winner moves into a three-way tie for first place in the ACC. "It'll be one of the louder games we play," Pitt head coach Pat Narduzzi said this week. Here are three bold predictions for the game. 1. Jeffrey Overton Jr. runs for 100 yards on the nation's No. 4 run defense Pitt has allowed 213 rushing yards in four games. Overton ran for 209 yards last Saturday at Boston College, including the 76-yard touchdown that put Virginia Tech ahead for good in a 21-14 win. That earned him ACC Running Back of the Week. The sophomore missed the first eight games of last season with an injury and finished 2025 with 25 carries. He already has 60 this fall, for 409 yards and four rushing touchdowns at 6.8 yards per carry. He'll run Friday without left tackle Justin Terry, who is out. That's a real problem against a defense allowing 53.3 rushing yards per game. 2. Mason Heintschel leaves Blacksburg without a touchdown pass Pitt's sophomore quarterback has thrown 13 touchdown passes, second in the ACC. Seven came against Miami (Ohio). Six came against Bucknell. Against UCF and Syracuse, he went 28 of 52 for 335 yards with no touchdowns and an interception. The Panthers got past Syracuse by running for 245 yards, and true freshman running back Damon Ferguson Jr. leads the team with 239 yards for the season. Virginia Tech has to take that away first. Then comes the hard part for Heintschel. This is his first road start of the season, against a defense that leads the nation with 45 tackles for loss and 17 sacks. The risk sits behind Virginia Tech's front. Maryland threw for 359 yards and three touchdowns on the Hokies two weeks ago, and Virginia Tech has one interception in four games. Defensive coordinator Brent Pry's group doesn't have to be perfect. It has to make Heintschel uncomfortable, and no defense in the country has lived in the backfield more. 3. John Love hits a walk-off field goal, and Virginia Tech is ranked by Sunday John Love has scored 313 points in a Virginia Tech uniform. The next three decide Friday night. "This is going to be a battle," Virginia Tech head coach James Franklin said Monday. Franklin would know. He faced Narduzzi four times from 2016-19 when he was at Penn State. Pitt leads the ACC at 8.5 points allowed per game and hasn't given up more than 14 to anyone. I have Virginia Tech get past that number, but not by much. The Panthers stay in it on the ground, the way they did against Syracuse. That leaves it to Love. The fifth-year kicker is fourth on Virginia Tech's all-time scoring list, has a career-long of 60 yards, and went 2 for 2 at Boston College. He gets one more with the clock running out. Virginia Tech wins 24-21. The Hokies have 86 points in the AP poll, fifth among teams outside the Top 25, and haven't been ranked since 2021.With a win on Friday night, it will be hard to leave them out for another week. picks.blurb: Full Game Preview and Score Prediction for Virginia Tech vs. Pitt - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus 49ers owner suspended, fined WNBA playoffs CBS, Tony Romo part ways Browns outlast Steelers Duren, Pistons reach deal Full Game Preview and Score Prediction for Virginia Tech vs. Pitt Virginia Tech Athletics Thomas Hughes Fri, October 2, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads BLACKSBURG, Va. - For the first time in 20 days, Virginia Tech football hosts a game at Lane Stadium - this one against Pitt with a 5-0 start hanging in the balance. Both the Hokies (4-0, 1-0 ACC) and Panthers (4-0, 1-0 ACC) enter Friday night's contest with unblemished marks, making the matchup one of four games nationally this week between undefeated FBS teams. For Virginia Tech, a victory would secure its first 5-0 start since 2005 and continue a remarkable turnaround in James Franklin's first season at the helm. Virginia Tech's perfect record hasn't come without adversity. After opening the season with commanding victories over VMI (73-3) and Old Dominion (44-21), the Hokies survived consecutive road tests against Maryland and Boston College . Tech defeated the Terrapins 35-26 before escaping a rain-soaked Chestnut Hill with a 21-14 victory. The latter required Virginia Tech to overcome a 14-6 fourth-quarter deficit. Quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer led an 80-yard touchdown drive that ended with a 14-yard score to Marlion Jackson, and Jeffrey Overton Jr. broke free for a 76-yard touchdown less than three minutes later to put the Hokies ahead for good. Overton's emergence has added another dimension to an offense that relied heavily on Grunkemeyer through the first three weeks. The sophomore enters Friday with 409 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 60 carries, averaging 6.8 yards per attempt. He erupted for a career-high 209 yards on 25 carries against Boston College, earning ACC Running Back of the Week honors. Finding similar success against Pitt, though, will be difficult. The Panthers enter Blacksburg allowing just 53.3 rushing yards per game and 8.5 points per contest. Pitt's defense has surrendered just 34 points through four games, following a 59-14 win over Miami (Ohio) with victories of 12-7 over UCF, 27-13 over Syracuse and 59-0 over Bucknell. That creates perhaps the game's most important matchup. Virginia Tech has found a potential difference-maker in Overton, but Pitt possesses one of the stingiest rushing defenses in the country. If the Panthers can prevent Overton from consistently reaching the second level, more responsibility will fall back onto Grunkemeyer. The Penn State transfer has largely handled that responsibility well. Grunkemeyer has completed 101 of 136 passes for 1,012 yards, eight touchdowns and no interceptions through four games. Boston College limited him to 147 passing yards, but the weather played a significant factor. Pitt quarterback Mason Heintschel has completed 88 of 130 passes for 1,191 yards, 13 touchdowns and just one interception. His season began with a historic seven-touchdown performance against Miami (Ohio), and he threw for 403 yards and six touchdowns in last week's demolition of Bucknell. Heintschel became the first ACC quarterback to record multiple six-touchdown passing games in the same season. That should provide Virginia Tech's pass rush with its biggest challenge yet. The Hokies have consistently disrupted opposing backfields, entering Friday averaging 4.25 sacks and 11.3 tackles for loss per game. Cortez Harris has led that charge with five sacks, including two in the victory over Boston College. Getting to Heintschel could be critical. Pitt averages 347.3 passing yards and 39.3 points per game, and its passing attack isn't dependent on a single target. Thirteen different Panthers caught a pass against Bucknell, while five players hauled in touchdowns. Censere Lee led the scoring barrage with three touchdown receptions. Friday also represents something Pitt hasn't experienced this season: a road game. The Panthers played each of their first four contests at Acrisure Stadium and now head into a sold-out Lane Stadium for a primetime matchup. Pitt is 3-8 all-time in Blacksburg, although the Panthers have won three of the last four overall meetings between the programs. Virginia Tech won the most recent matchup, 38-21, in 2023. Virginia Tech has answered four different tests through four weeks. Pitt presents another, and perhaps the most complete one yet. One undefeated record will disappear Friday night. Which one do I think will? Virginia Tech's defense should give Pitt its toughest test yet, while Lane Stadium could make the Panthers' first road game uncomfortable. The Hokies may not completely contain Heintschel, but Overton and Grunkemeyer should generate enough offense late to preserve the unbeaten start in a tightly contested ACC matchup. Virginia Tech Athleticse Thomas Hughes Fri, October 2, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads BLACKSBURG, Va. - Virginia Tech football takes on Pitt tomorrow night in its fifth contest of the 2026 season. Ahead of the Friday evening clash against the Panthers, three members of our staff offered their thoughts on what could unfold tomorrow: JACKSON CAUDELL: This is the biggest Virginia Tech game in years. If they win, they will be 5-0 and have a win against one of the teams expected to compete for a spot in the ACC Championship game, giving them a huge tiebreaker. You could argue that the winner of this game is going to be in the best position to make it to Charlotte and likely face Miami . I expect this to be a close game, but the home-field advantage and Virginia Tech's defense are going to be the difference. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 24, Pitt 20 JAMES DUNCAN: Nobody has scored on Pitt in the first or third quarter this season. The Panthers allow 8.5 points per game, fewest in the ACC. Against a Virginia Tech line missing left tackle Justin Terry, I don't see the Hokies hanging 40. Expect quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer to live on quick throws to tight end Luke Reynolds. But Pitt has been flagged 37 times for 359 yards, all at home. Now its first road trip is Lane Stadium on a Friday night. If pre-snap penalties have been an issue at home, who knows what it will be in front of 65,000 people screaming at the top of their lungs when trying to hear a snap count. I still expect this game to come down to the final snap. In fact, I'm predicting a walk-off field goal from John Love to give James Franklin his signature moment in his first season at Virginia Tech. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 24, Pitt 21 THOMAS HUGHES: Virginia Tech has an opportunity to turn a promising start into a true renaissance Friday night. Pitt presents a challenge on defense, and the Hokies will need to help Ethan Grunkemeyer avoid spending the evening under pressure. Quick throws to Luke Reynolds and a productive rushing attack should be central to that effort, and they should be more available than in last Saturday's rainy affair in Chestnut Hill. Still, I trust Virginia Tech to find enough offense to keep this game within reach throughout. The bigger question is whether the Hokies can force Pitt into the mistakes that become increasingly costly in a close conference matchup. Lane Stadium should have something to say about that, particularly if the Panthers struggle with penalties. I expect a competitive game that remains undecided into the fourth quarter, but that Virginia Tech's defense delivers the final stop to keep James Franklin's team unbeaten and firmly in the ACC conversation. picks.blurb: Virginia Tech Hokies vs. Pittsburgh Panthers: News, Updates, and Predictions | Gobbler Country Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Virginia Tech Hokies Community Gobbler Country October 3, 2026 Gobbler Country Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Virginia Tech Football Virginia Tech Basketball Virginia Tech Baseball Betting FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Virginia Tech Football Odds Virginia Tech Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Virginia Tech Football Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Virginia Tech Football Virginia Tech hosts the Pittsburgh Panthers in an old fashioned Big East grudge match. Tech is a narrow homefield favorite, but the media and commentariat don’t agree. It’s looking like a season where the upcoming game is the most important game of the season. If you had to pick a really obvious one out of the stack, the Pitt game runs right to the top of the flagpole. Let’s look at some team news, a few updates here and there, and then get to the predictions. It’s not Homecoming, but It is Stripe Lane Night The program has fan gimmicks for most games this season, and it’s a night where certain sections wear orange, and others wear maroon. Sometimes it works out, and sometimes it sort of looks like more than half the people didn’t care or didn’t know. Just a Reminder that the Team in Maroon Earned Its Way Last Saturday in a New England coastal Nor’easter, the Hokies earned their respect the hard way, by fighting BC and the weather to catch, pass, and then burn out the clock before they had a chance to respond. Jeffrey Overton, Jr. Gets Some Kudos He gets named ACC Running Back of the Week for his powerful performance in the rain and wind of Alumni Stadium. PFF picks out Overton but also adds Quentin Reddish and Jaquez White for their National Team of the Week notice. Catch Up with Coach Franklin’s Weekly Presser This is nearly a 51-minute watch so go grab a coffee. Lots of good information in this one. Predictions Time Huge game for the Hokies. This game means a lot for several reasons. A chance to go 5-0, a chance to go 2-0 in the ACC, a chance to re-establish Lane Stadium as a place that visiting teams dread coming to play. Pitt is a tough challenge. Under Pat Narduzzi, the Panthers always play a tough brand of football. They generally play solid defense and rely on the running game. They now have a quarterback who can air it out. Pitt’s strengths and Virginia Tech’s potential weaknesses match up well for the Panthers. The Hokies have allowed some big plays through the air this year, so Pitt will test that. I have concerns about Pitt’s run defense. The Hokies have had some issues at times this year and are dealing with multiple injuries along the offensive line. That’s something to watch. I do think the Hokies will make some plays in the running game. More Jeffrey Overton, please. Luke Reynolds had a down game last week, due to the weather more than anything, but I expect a big bounce-back this week. Reynolds catches another touchdown and quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer is the better quarterback on the field again this week. It’s close, but the Hokies win. Virginia Tech 27, Pitt 21 Tough games require some tough thinking. This one is essentially a toss-up, and regardless of these two teams’ records they always seem to be a fist fight street brawl. This season neither team is ranked, but neither is showing up at Lane Stadium with a loss on their record. Tech is rallying up behind a completely revamped and very different offense than we have seen since the Michael Brewer days at the end of the Beamer Era. This Tech team has an actual quarterback, uses its tight ends and gets downfield with intermediate distance pass plays. The defensive style isn’t much different than has been fielded in the past, but the line is bigger and a bit faster than we are used to. It still has problems with running quarterbacks, and the secondary has just not stiffened yet. That’s a concern for this one because Nardo has found a good quarterback, too, and as we saw in the recent past when he has a good quarterback his teams go from wobbly to competitive. To win this Tech has to drive and score on nearly every possession. The defense needs to get fast “A” gap pressure on Pitt’s QB, and the secondary needs to stiffen up considerably. It’s also going to need to avoid any “prevent” situations since Pitt can score fast if it needs to. Add all that stuff up, and this one is going to be one of two things. A runaway with one team dominating over the other with fast offensive and heavy defensive pressure, or both teams are going to force a tough close contest. I am thinking the latter is more likely, I still have pictures in the library of the 4th quarter 4th and Goal for Pitt at the Tech 2. This stacks up to be, in my mind anyway, a similar contest. I think Tech takes it, but it’s going to be close, a 3- or 4-point difference. Both teams are probably good for scores in the mid- to high- twenties. The team that breaks 30 wins. 31 - 24 Hokies Just a Reminder About Friday Evening If you are coming to the game, check your seat against the chart, and wear the appropriate color. We’ll be on the field, cameras going, stay with us for pictures on the Facebook page Saturday evening. GO HOKIES!!!! away.blurb: Defensive end Zach Crothers and tight end Elijah Lagg have both been listed as doubtful to play against the Hokies. Receiver Tony Kinsler has been upgraded to probable after being tabbed as questionable on Wednesday. Safety Cruce Brookins is still questionable to suit up. Two new players have popped up on the availability report for Pitt on Thursday night ahead of Friday night’s clash with Virginia Tech in Blacksburg. picks.blurb: Penn State vs. Northwestern Predictions: Week 5 Stress Test for Nittany Lions Skip to main content SI.COM OLYMPIC SPORTS 2025 Football Bracket FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS A year ago, James Franklin walked off the Beaver Stadium field for the last time after Penn State's 22-21 loss to Northwestern. The Wildcats turned a fourth-quarter drive into the game-winning touchdown that ended Franklin's tenure as Penn State's head coach. On Friday night, the Nittany Lions get another crack at the Wildcats, this time as part of a grand opening. Northwestern will host Penn State in the first game at the new Ryan Field, a nearly $900 million venue that claims to be the most expensive college stadium ever built. There are plenty of Penn State storylines Friday night beyond a mostly new program getting proxy retribution for last year's loss at Beaver Stadium. More than half of Penn State's roster wasn't on the field that night and doesn't care about settling scores. These Nittany Lions want to settle their offense. With that in mind, here's how we see Friday's Penn State-Northwestern game shaking out, including our predictions from the Penn State on SI staff. Kickoff is scheduled for just after 8 p..m. ET on FOX. 1. Penn State vs. Northwestern game predictions Penn State Nittany Lions quarterback Rocco Becht (3) gestures at the line of scrimmage against the Wisconsin Badgers at Beaver Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Chase Fisher: A movable object (Penn State’s inconsistent rush offense) meets a stoppable force (Northwestern’s second-worst Big Ten rush defense) Friday. If the Nittany Lions’ rushing attack finally shows signs of life, it’s going to be hard for the Wildcats defense, which allows 417.3 yards per game, to get stops. Penn State bounces back in a big way and silences a likely raucous Northwestern crowd. Penn State 31, Northwestern 17 Chase Fisher: A movable object (Penn State’s inconsistent rush offense) meets a stoppable force (Northwestern’s second-worst Big Ten rush defense) Friday. If the Nittany Lions’ rushing attack finally shows signs of life, it’s going to be hard for the Wildcats defense, which allows 417.3 yards per game, to get stops. Penn State bounces back in a big way and silences a likely raucous Northwestern crowd. Penn State 31, Northwestern 17 Will Horstman: It’s difficult to trust Penn State’s offense after its lackluster performance against Wisconsin, and I don’t see it getting easier in the Northwestern game. Even before the season, this game was circled as a tricky road matchup with the Wildcats opening their new stadium. The Nittany Lions’ defense will likely keep them close, but there’s too many questions for the offense to expect a win. Northwestern 21, Penn State 17 Mark Wogenrich: Penn State’s offensive showing (yes, it was) against Wisconsin, particularly that of quarterback Rocco Becht, should be an anomaly. Sure, the Nittany Lions are understaffed in the explosives department without Koby Howard, but there’s no way they can be that ineffective two weeks straight. Right? James Peoples thinks Penn State can run on Northwestern . We do too. Penn State 27, Northwestern 14 2. Who will be the game's MVP? Penn State Nittany Lions linebacker Tony Rojas (13) reacts after intercepting a pass against the Wisconsin Badgers at Beaver Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Chase Fisher: Running back James Peoples said Wednesday that the Northwestern rush defense can be run on. He backs his word against the Wildcats Friday, rushes for at least 125 yards and a touchdown, and firmly grasps the lead-back role in a Penn State offense that needs him badly. Chase Fisher: Running back James Peoples said Wednesday that the Northwestern rush defense can be run on. He backs his word against the Wildcats Friday, rushes for at least 125 yards and a touchdown, and firmly grasps the lead-back role in a Penn State offense that needs him badly. Will Horstman: Penn State linebacker Tony Rojas has played some good football since returning from his ACL injury. Despite the loss to Wisconsin, he stuck out with six tackles (two for loss), a sack and an interception. Even if Penn State loses again to Northwestern, I don’t think it’ll be because of the defense. Rojas likely would continue his standout season against the Wildcats. Mark Wogenrich: Speaking of James Peoples, he’s been a confident personality on the roster. The Ohio State transfer said he expected to see the Buckeyes again this season and then called last week’s loss a necessary evil . Peoples backs that up at Northwestern with a 100-yard game. 3. Who is the game's unsung hero? Penn State Nittany Lions wide receiver Brett Eskildsen reacts after scoring a touchdown against the Marshall Thundering Herd at Beaver Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Chase Fisher: Wide receiver Brett Eskildsen has to break out sometime soon, right? He hasn’t eclipsed 50 yards in a game yet but almost made a big impact against Wisconsin, cleanly beating a Badger cornerback for what would’ve been a nearly 50-yard touchdown if quarterback Rocco Becht didn’t overthrow him. Those two should finally connect Friday and Eskildsen will find himself in the end zone. Chase Fisher: Wide receiver Brett Eskildsen has to break out sometime soon, right? He hasn’t eclipsed 50 yards in a game yet but almost made a big impact against Wisconsin, cleanly beating a Badger cornerback for what would’ve been a nearly 50-yard touchdown if quarterback Rocco Becht didn’t overthrow him. Those two should finally connect Friday and Eskildsen will find himself in the end zone. Will Horstman: Offensive coordinator Taylor Mouser said he wants to get his tight ends more involved. This should lead to tight end Ben Brahmer to see more action against Northwestern, as he could be who the offense turns to for better production after the passing game lacked a rhythm against Wisconsin. Mark Wogenrich: Receiver Brett Eskildsen hasn’t jumped out of the gate at Penn State. He was hurt through camp and the non-conference schedule and went 0-for-6 on targets against Wisconsin. Eskildsen emerges with some key catches Friday, including a deep shot. 4. What major change will Penn State's offense make? Penn State Nittany Lions quarterback Rocco Becht (3) runs with the ball against the Wisconsin Badgers at Beaver Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Chase Fisher: Becht will have all the time in the world in the pocket Friday, and the running game will have gaping holes, thanks to an offensive line blocking “fix” Peoples said that unit was working on. Because of this, Penn State’s offense has its most efficient, well-balanced game of the season, throwing for at least 250 yards and rushing for at least 200 yards. Because of this, Penn State’s offense has its most efficient, well-balanced game of the season, throwing for at least 250 yards and rushing for at least 200 yards. Will Horstman: Penn State had four running backs involved in the first quarter against Wisconsin. I don’t think that will happen again as the Nittany Lions should tighten up their running back rotation. If that happens, expect running back James Peoples to see the majority of carries, as he received praise after being the most productive rusher last week. Mark Wogenrich: Accuracy has never headlined Rocco Becht’s resume. He’s a career 61-percent passer who has dipped below that 19 times in his career. That includes the last two weeks, notably his 41-percent completion rate vs. the Badgers. Maybe his noncon start was the outlier, but Becht is better than he was last week and will get some of his juice back. 5. What will Penn State fans be talking about Saturday? Penn State Nittany Lions head coach Matt Campbell walks on the field following the game against the Buffalo Bulls at Beaver Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Chase Fisher: Are the playoffs back on? Penn State will spoil Northwestern’s first game in its new stadium and give fans hope again. A struggling USC defense and a not-so-impressive Michigan team will be on deck. Nittany Lions fans will be convinced Penn State could pull off a sweep. Chase Fisher: Are the playoffs back on? Penn State will spoil Northwestern’s first game in its new stadium and give fans hope again. A struggling USC defense and a not-so-impressive Michigan team will be on deck. Nittany Lions fans will be convinced Penn State could pull off a sweep. Will Horstman: It’s way too early to make any assumptions about how Campbell will perform during his time at Penn State, but another loss probably won’t stop fans from talking about that. If the Nittany Lions don’t get a win Friday, there could be more worrying about the future of the Campbell era, even though it's only Game 5 of Year 1. Photo By - Reuters Connect. Penn State Nittany Lions Northwestern Wildcats NCAAF Penn State travels to Evanston laying 2.5 points in a prime bounce-back spot. Despite Northwestern nearly upsetting Indiana, my Penn State vs. Northwestern prediction and college football picks hinges on Penn State dominating the trenches. Kickoff is set for 8 p.m. ET in Evanston, with the game airing on FOX. TOP PICK Who will win Penn State vs Northwestern: Penn State -2.5 I like Penn State up to -3 as a fade of last week's results. Penn State choked away a 10-point fourth-quarter lead in a 24-20 loss to Wisconsin, while Northwestern nearly upset reigning national champion Indiana on the road. That creates a natural let-down spot for the Wildcats, even if they are at home. More importantly, the Nittany Lions have a better net standard-down success rate and line yards differential, according to CollegeFootballData.com . Trench play and success rate on first and second downs are the two most predictive aspects in football handicapping , and both favor Penn State. Penn State vs Northwestern Over/Under pick: Under 46.5 The Under 46.5 is playable down to 45.5, with two slow-paced teams that like to pound the rock . Northwestern ranks 87th in offensive seconds per play , while Penn State is 104th, and both sit 34th in rushing rate against FBS opponents. Meanwhile, Wildcats QB Aidan Chiles has taken too many drive-killing sacks. Northwestern enters this one 113th in sack rate allowed and 127th in yards per rush against FBS opponents. Poor early-down rushing should put Chiles in long third-down situations, allowing Penn State to keep them from reaching the red zone. Penn State vs Northwestern combo I expect Penn State to punch first and control this game in the trenches , while Northwestern's weak rushing attack and sack problems should keep the scoring down. The Nittany Lions also own the standard-down advantage, which should help them stay ahead of the chains. I'm using Penn State's moneyline instead of its full-game spread to increase the win probability and protect against Northwestern's tendency to play its best football after halftime. Penn State moneyline Nittany Lions 1H -2.5 Penn State vs Northwestern prop: Penn State 1H -2.5 As long as Penn State's first-half spread stays below -3, I'm in. The Nittany Lions should come out strong after allowing 14 unanswered points in the fourth quarter of their loss to Wisconsin last week. Penn State averages 5.8 more points per game in the first half (21.3 to 15.5) , while the Wildcats more than double their first-half scoring output in the second half (21.5 to 10.5). picks.blurb: Week 5 Game Predictions: Northwestern Wildcats vs. Penn State - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAB March Madness Get Fantasy Plus 49ers owner suspended, fined WNBA playoffs CBS, Tony Romo part ways Browns outlast Steelers Duren, Pistons reach deal Week 5 Game Predictions: Northwestern Wildcats vs. Penn State Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Northwestern will return home Friday night when the Wildcats take on Penn State in the highly anticipated first game at New Ryan Field . Northwestern enters the matchup with a 2-1 record after falling just short in a 29-23 loss to No. 5 Indiana , while Penn State comes to Evanston at 3-1 after suffering a 24-20 loss to Wisconsin. The Wildcats will look to bounce back from their first loss of the season while beginning a new era in front of a large crowd. Penn State will also be looking to get back in the win column after allowing a 17-0 lead to slip away against the Badgers. The game is scheduled for 7 p.m. CT Friday at New Ryan Field and will air nationally on FOX. Here are our predictions for Friday's historic matchup. Alex Kwiatkowski (3-0): Northwestern 30, Penn State 24 I'm taking Northwestern to open the new Ryan Field era with a win. The Wildcats are starting to look like a team that can truly compete in the Big Ten. Northwestern entered last week as a 23.5-point underdog against No. 5 Indiana but nearly pulled off the upset, eventually falling 29-23 in Bloomington. What impressed me most was how Northwestern responded after a terrible first half. The Wildcats trailed 12-0 at halftime but refused to go away, scoring 23 points in the second half and putting themselves in position to potentially win the game late. Aidan Chiles continues to look comfortable in Chip Kelly's offense, and Northwestern has shown it has multiple weapons in the passing game. Chiles threw for 293 yards and accounted for three touchdowns against Indiana, while Luke Dehnicke and Griffin Wilde combined for 196 receiving yards. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images Now, Northwestern gets to return home with plenty of excitement surrounding the program. Friday will mark the first game at New Ryan Field, and the stadium is sold out. I expect the Wildcats to feed off the energy and come out hot in front of what should be one of the best home atmospheres Northwestern has experienced in years. Penn State, meanwhile, enters at a low point after blowing a 17-0 lead in a 24-20 loss to Wisconsin. The Nittany Lions will be motivated to bounce back, but I think Northwestern carries its momentum from the second half against Indiana into Friday night. I expect Chiles and the offense to put points on the board early, while the defense does enough to keep Penn State from finding a consistent rhythm. Northwestern begins its new era with a statement win. Prediction: Northwestern 30, Penn State 24 Nick Meyer (2-0): Penn State 27, Northwestern 24 The Wildcats looked like a Big Ten title contender on the road against Indiana last week, while Penn State was upset at home by Wisconsin. I expect Northwestern to be fired up for the opening game at New Ryan Field, but I also expect the Wildcats to make a few mistakes due to the emotions and jitters surrounding such a historic night. This should be another close game, but Northwestern is expected to be without tight end Luke Dehnicke, who had a huge performance against Indiana with seven receptions for 140 yards. His absence would take away one of Aidan Chiles' most productive targets. This is a winnable game for Northwestern, but I expect Penn State to have the advantage in the trenches on both sides of the ball. Ultimately, that will be enough for the Nittany Lions to escape Evanston with a close win. Prediction: Penn State 27, Northwestern 24

picks.blurb: Penn State Given Interesting Prediction Ahead of Northwestern Matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAB March Madness Get Fantasy Plus 49ers owner suspended, fined WNBA playoffs CBS, Tony Romo part ways Browns outlast Steelers Duren, Pistons reach deal Penn State Given Interesting Prediction Ahead of Northwestern Matchup (Matthew O'Haren-Imagn Images) Matt Levine Thu, October 1, 2026 at 8:17 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Penn State Nittany Lions will be looking to get back on track tomorrow against Northwestern , in what could be a tough game for the team. Penn State fell 24-20 to Wisconsin last week in what was one of the more surprising scores from the weekend. But the Nittany Lions believe that the loss to the Badgers was more of an outlier, and this team still has a lot to play for this year. As the team gets ready for the Wildcats, the Nittany Lions will need to make sure that they don't overlook them. Northwestern has played much better to start the season than they have in year's past, opening the year 2-1 under head coach David Braun. For Penn State, this can be a bounce-back game, with the team getting things right after the tough loss against Wisconsin. But Friday night games can be tough, especially having to go on the road. Heading into the game, the Nittany Lions are favored to win the contest, but not by too much. According to ESPN , Penn State is being given a 55.9 percent chance to take down Northwestern on the road. If the Nittany Lions are going to win this game, everything starts and end with quarterback Rocco Becht . Becht has looked good to open the year, throwing for 865 yards with nine touchdowns and one interception. But against the Badgers, Becht struggled, throwing for just 114 yards and one interception. The veteran signal-caller will need to get back on track in this game against Northwestern if the Nittany Lions are to have a shot at winning. Coming over from Iowa State with head coach Matt Campbell, Becht gives Penn State a legitimate option under center. But he has bene prone to some inconsistency at times during his career, and last week was one of those moments for him. Northwestern has its own star quarterback in Aidan Chiles , who transferred to the team this offseason. So far, Chiles has played very well for the Wildcats, throwing for 807 yards with six touchdowns and no interceptions. If Penn State can find a way to slow him down, it could make life much easier to grab the win. But Chiles has turned this offense around, and this will be something that the Nittany Lions will need to focus on throughout the game. Overall, Penn State needs to take down Northwestern if they want a chance to make the College Football Playoff this year. The Nittany Lions are off to a good a start this year, even with the loss last week, and this game offers them a chance to turn the page.

On the other hand, Penn State is merely looking to rebound after a tough loss at home last week to Wisconsin that saw the Nittany Lions blow a double-digit lead in the fourth quarter. This week, there can be no excuse for not having something going in the passing game. I think that means Rocco Becht needs to get into a comfort zone with his tight ends a bit more instead of looking for some big plays down the field from the receivers. So for the second week in a row, I'm looking for Ben BRahmer to be a difference maker for the offense. If Penn State can get that, then they should be in good enough shape to get out of Evanston with a hard-fought win. Northwestern will not make anything easy on the Nittany Lions. This may need to be a bit of a scrappy win from the offense. This time, it's on the road as Northwestern opens up the new Ryan Field. In order to spoil affairs, the Nittany Lions have to get going in the passing game and take advantage of what could be an aggressive Wildcat defense. Look for Chase Sowell to step up in the continued absence of Koby Howard and be the difference in a game that could come down to the last few plays. Follow Nittany Lions Wire on X and Facebook . home.blurb: Penn State DB questionable for Northwestern game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Penn State DB questionable for Northwestern game After last week's news surrounding the injury status of Koby Howard , Penn State fans could be forgiven for not wanting to hear anymore bad news. Now though, a pivotal defensive starter could miss some time as well. Sophomore cornerback Daryus Dixson apparently struggled with an injury during the Wisconsin game and is currently listed as questionable for the game against Northwestern . For Dixson, this could be a minor setback for what has been looking like a breakout season for the young corner. He recorded his first interception of the season last week and played the most snaps out of anyone on the defensive side of the ball. Most impressively, he has only allowed three receptions all season long, with the longest only being 16 yards. Against Buffalo, he also recorded a blocked field goal, proving his versatility and importance to the squad. While Dixson should be good to go should he miss the Northwestern game, others are not as lucky. Defensive end Max Granville suffered a season-ending injury in the first game of the season, his second in as many years. As for Koby Howard , no one knows when he will likely return, but to expect him to only miss a couple of games would be wishful thinking. Penn State fans can only hope this Dixson injury is the last of its kind this season. The Crimson Tide moved to 4-0 with a devastatingly dominant 49-18 win against South Carolina . Sophomore quarterback Keelon Russell was flawless with 365 yards passing and four touchdowns. Mississippi State is in the midst of one of the great starts in program history, reaching consecutive 4-0 starts for the first time since World War II. The Bulldogs came from behind to stun No. 19 Missouri 31-24 behind 360 yards and three touchdowns from superstar quarterback Kamario Taylor . Alabama has dominated the matchup between these two teams all-time, holding an 86-18-3 advantage, including a 40-17 win in 2023. However, the last MSU win came in Nick Saban's first season -- can the Bulldogs turn the Tide? Alabama vs. Mississippi State: Need to know Super Kamario: Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor has been the story of the early college football season. The Macon, Mississippi, native dreamed of playing in Starkville, and leads the SEC with 344.3 yards of offense per game. Taylor has thrown for at least three touchdowns in every start, including in road trips to Minnesota and South Carolina. With him in the lineup, suddenly anything seems possible at Mississippi State. Russell's rise: Taylor might be the best quarterback in the nation; he also might not be the best quarterback in this game. Since throwing a pair of interceptions in his first SEC start against Kentucky , Russell has been astonishing, throwing for 685 yards and seven touchdowns on 77% completion in wins over Florida State and South Carolina. Behind Russell's explosion, Alabama leads the nation in points per game against Power Four competition at 48.0 points per game. Best on worst: With so much attention on the quarterbacks, the secondaries will take center stage. Mississippi State has the worst passing defense in the SEC statistically, but the Bulldogs rank ahead of the Tide in both yards per attempt and passer rating allowed. Mississippi State has recorded nine sacks in four games, but getting a consistent pass rush could change the game. Davis Wade Stadium will be packed. The Bulldogs have a better running game to surround Kamario Taylor. They've played more competitive games to build resilience. But like so many Alabama games before, the Tide will just find a way to pull away at the end in perhaps the best quarterback battle of the season. picks.headline: Mississippi State vs. Alabama Prediction, TV Channel, Kickoff Time, Everything Fans Need to Know
picks.blurb: Mississippi State vs. Alabama Prediction, TV Channel, Kickoff Time, Everything Fans Need to Know Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THINGS STATE SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS STARKVILLE — It's been nearly two decades since Mississippi State felt the joy of a win against Alabama. Sylvester Croom was roaming the sidelines as first-year coach Nick Saban and his Crimson Tide program were in the midst of a late season slide. Fast-forward 20 years and its Kalen DeBoer leading the way, looking to lead his team to 5-0 record for the first time in his tenure. On the flip side, Mississippi State coach Jeff Lebby is looking to earn the first signature win of his young head coaching career while hosting No. 7 ranked Alabama for a nationally televised showdown on ABC. Here's everything you need to know to be prepared for what's a pivotal weekend for the Bulldogs program. Mississippi State Bulldogs running back Fluff Bothwell (24) and wide receiver Zion Ragins (7) react after a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Missouri Tigers at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Game Information Game Information Mississippi State vs. Alabama Crimson Tide When : Saturday, Oct. 3, 2026 Kickoff Time : 11 a.m. CT Venue : Davis Wade Stadium, Starkville, Mississippi TV Channel : ABC Radio : Bulldogs Sports Network Series Record : Alabama leads 86-18-3 Betting : Alabama (-5.5), O/u: 60.5 total points ( FanDuel ) DISCLAIMER : Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. What ESPN Thinks The brand of Alabama remains strong on the national radar and that's no different this week at ESPN with the Crimson Tide given a 74.2% chance of going into one of the most hostile atmospheres in all of college football and pulling out a win, according to ESPN's Football Power Index . Mississippi State State continues its climb up the FPI rating system, coming in this week at No. 9 among SEC teams and No. 20 overall with key victories on the road at Minnesota and South Carolina plus another against then No. 19 Missouri. This starts one of the stiffest stretches for any team as the Bulldogs are set for a murderer's row-level slate with Alabama coming Saturday, proceeded by a BYE, on the road at LSU, home against Oklahoma and then another road trip to Austin to face the Texas Longhorns. The Bulldogs chances of winning out are slim at 0.1%, but do have a 97.5% chance of at least reaching bowl eligibility with six wins. When it comes to making the playoffs, Lebby's team has the sixth-best odds SEC teams at 23.8% to at least make the field, 1.6% to make the championship game and 0.5% chance to win the national championship. ESPN FPI (SEC) Rankings 1. Georgia 2. Texas 3. Alabama 4. LSU 5. Florida 6. Tennessee 7. Texas A&M 8. Ole Miss 9. Mississippi State 10. Oklahoma 11. Auburn 12. South Carolina 13. Missouri 14. Kentucky 15. Vanderbilt 16. Arkansas Alabama Crimson Tide head coach Kalen DeBoer walks off the field after a victory against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What DeBoer Is Saying What DeBoer Is Saying One of the hardest things for a coach to prepare his team for in a road game at Davis-Wade Stadium is the cadence of cowbells. Thousands of cowbells. "Personally, this is one of those stadiums that I haven't played in no matter where I've been," DeBoer said Monday. "What I hear from the people that I trust, is that it's going to be an absolutely crazy environment. We're going to be prepared for that. We talked about as a team this morning and we're looking forward to that challenge. "We know, this week, we've got to work on that crowd noise. There will probably be a lot of cowbells that we're hearing in practice in one form or fashion. Another thing is that it's just an early game. It's an 11 o'clock kickoff. We're a morning practice team and we've had some success in those morning games. We've got to go on the road and travel that morning. It's going to be a little different set-up that way too." The Bulldogs' defense has been very active this season at stopping explosive plays and keeping everything in front of them. They're disciplined, bring elite energy and effort with each down. "They play complementary football. They get the ball back, get off the field and get the ball back to the offense. I think it's timely stops. It's a group effort of guys flying around. They're going to be multiple in what they show you. "I have a lot of respect for them and what they are doing this time of the year. I think complementary football is what they're doing really well at Mississippi State. They're explosive. Obviously, that defense has to face that offense every day in practice. It's high level across the board." Mississippi State Bulldogs head coach Jeff Lebby looks on during the second quarter against the Missouri Tigers at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What Lebby Is Saying What Lebby Is Saying The Crimson Tide offense is full of big play athletes at nearly every position. Whether that's done with Keelon Russell's dual-threat combination, a four-headed backfield, Ryan Williams or any other weapon, Lebby knows his defense has to play assignment-driven, technically sound football to avoid allowing the game to get away from them early. "We're gonna have to do a great job tackling," Lebby said. "That's gonna be a huge piece of it. He's played really well. He's been incredibly productive. There's been explosive plays. He's got great talent around him. And so for us it's going to be about applying pressure, getting our fans really involved and excited about what's going on in between those white lines. "So for us it's kinda like I mentioned. We gotta get him off the spot and we've got to do a great job taking air out of it on the back end and making the plays when we get the chance." Alabama is tied for No. 24 nationally in sacks with 11 on the season. On the otherhand, Mississippi State has given up nine sacks on the season, which ranks No. 9 nationally, but the most alarming number was the four given up against Missouri in last week's 31-24 victory. And Lebby knows the biggest key to the Bulldogs upset bid will be keeping star quarterback Kamario Taylor upright to further establish himself as a Heisman Trophy contender. “[We] had moments where we were really clean, and had moments where we’ve got to continue to clean up,” Lebby said. “The fundamental pieces of it I’m gonna continue to talk about. Those guys playing clean fundamentally gives us the best chance to protect 1, but there were issues from a game standpoint. "We didn’t do a great job on the penetrator a couple times, and that’s part of being able to clean that up as we watch the tape, a huge focus for us this week.” Prediction : Mississippi State 42, Alabama 38 Loading recommendations... picks.blurb: Former UCLA Coach Rick Neuheisel Predicts Winner of Alabama-Mississippi State Game Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS No. 7 Alabama (4-0, 2-0) travels to Davis Wade Stadium to face No. 16 Mississippi State (4-0, 2-0) in the SEC's lone ranked matchup of Week 5 (Noon EDT, ABC). These two programs are separated by an hour and a half's driving distance and are meeting for the first time in three seasons. Alabama and Mississippi State have been traditional staples on each other's schedules, although the 86-18-3 advantage held by the Crimson Tide makes for the most lopsided series in SEC history. The Bulldogs' last victory was in 2007, Nick Saban's first season in Tuscaloosa. The closest Mississippi State came within the last 16 meetings was in 2017; the game was tied in the final 30 seconds, and Jalen Hurts hit then-freshman wide receiver DeVonta Smith for a 26-yard touchdown pass to win it 31-24. The matchup features a pair of high-octane offenses Sep 26, 2026; Tuscaloosa, Alabama, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell (12) throws the ball during the first quarter against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Alabama has scored 45 points or more in each of its first four games. The Crimson Tide did run back interceptions for touchdowns in three of those four, but that means the offense has scored no fewer than 38 points in a game to start the season. Alabama has scored 45 points or more in each of its first four games. The Crimson Tide did run back interceptions for touchdowns in three of those four, but that means the offense has scored no fewer than 38 points in a game to start the season. Keelon Russell has been fantastic for Alabama, but the most impressive part of the offense is the run game. The Crimson Tide has been questionable in that department for the better part of three seasons, and it has very quickly found a combination of offensive linemen and running backs to correct the deficiency. On the other side, Kamario Taylor has lived up to the hype for Mississippi State. He guided the Bulldogs to a pair of road wins at Minnesota and South Carolina to bring excitement to a fan base desperate for optimism, and he delivered a 31-24 win over Missouri to a packed Davis Wade Stadium under the lights in Week 4. Neuheisel: "I see two matchups here that are really cool." CBS Sports' "Inside College Football" panel predicted the winner of the game between Alabama and Mississippi State on Tuesday. Former UCLA head coach Rick Neuheisel pointed to a pair of critical matchups between the Crimson Tide and Bulldogs while making his game pick. "Number one is the quarterbacks," Neuheisel said . "These two guys are both going to play on Sundays, both have just unique frames. They're 19 years old and they're just getting started." Despite the intrigue in the quarterback matchup, Neuheisel pointed to the other matchup as a deciding factor due to the current weather forecast for Saturday. "The second matchup is between the two defensive coordinators," Neuheisel said. "Both have been head coaches: Kane Wommack was at South Alabama, Zach Arnett was ironically right here at Mississippi State, these guys know how to play field position defense. It's supposed to rain a lot during the game, I think I've got to go, in that situation with Alabama." Loading recommendations... picks.blurb: Alabama Receives Nerve-Wracking Prediction vs Mississippi State - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus 49ers owner suspended, fined WNBA playoffs CBS, Tony Romo part ways Browns outlast Steelers Duren, Pistons reach deal Alabama Receives Nerve-Wracking Prediction vs Mississippi State (David Leong-Imagn Images) Matthew Schmidt Thu, October 1, 2026 at 1:32 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Alabama Crimson Tide are coming off of a dominant Week 4 win over South Carolina, which represented their most complete performance all season. Now, Alabama is preparing for its most difficult test yet , as the Crimson Tide are heading on the road to battle the upstart Mississippi State Bulldogs this Saturday. Like Alabama, Mississippi State is 4-0, and the Bulldogs are also fresh off of a very impressive victory, having topped Missouri last weekend. Mississippi State boasts an explosive offense, and while its defense certainly isn't among the best, it has a pair of terrific cornerbacks in Kelley Jones and Jett Jefferson that could pose some problems for Keelon Russell and Co. So, are the Crimson Tide on upset alert heading into Week 5? ESPN's Bill Connelly predicted the final score of the matchup using his SP+ metrics, and while he does have Alabama coming out on top, he thinks it will be a nail-biter, projecting a 32-27 win for the Tide in Starkville. A victory would absolutely comprise Alabama's most impressive of the campaign to date and would set Kalen DeBoer's squad up very nicely as it continues to proceed into the most challenging part of its schedule, which begins with the clash against the Bulldogs. While the Crimson Tide are undefeated, things haven't necessarily been easy for them thus far. Alabama took care of business without breaking a sweat against East Carolina in its season opener, but it trailed Kentucky 17-13 at halftime in Week 2 before dominating the second half. It also fell behind Florida State 21-6 in the first half the following week, but ultimately rallied for a 50-36 victory. The Crimson Tide definitely avoided a slow start versus South Carolina last Saturday, taking a 35-3 lead at one point in a 49-18 triumph. One thing is for sure: the version of Alabama that showed up in Weeks 2 and 3 absolutely cannot expect to waltz into Mississippi State and emerge with a victory. The Bulldogs are a significantly better team than either Kentucky or South Carolina, and the Crimson Tide fall behind early, they could be in some serious trouble. Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor is one of the top Heisman Trophy candidates at the moment, and the Bulldogs also possess a terrific backfield led by Fluff Bothwell. Wide receiver Anthony Evans III has also been a fast riser, too. Alabama cannot mess around this weekend.

Despite all these numbers, Las Vegas is still a little suspicious of these two teams. FanDuel has opening odds of Alabama being a 4.5 point favorite over the Bulldogs with an Over/Under of 59.5 for a day game in Starkville. MISSISSIPPI STATE So far this season, the sportsbooks have pegged Missy State as tighter point spreads as well as decent sized Over/Under in each game. They are a split 2-2 against the Over/Under. Like most observers, the books figured on closer games against the Golden Gophers and the Gamecocks. But with the development of QB Kamario Taylor, the points have come much easier. Next, the Bulldogs face their first ranked team of the year. The Over/Unders for Bama thus far have not been big. Is it fair to say that the FSU game may have been a fluke or is that being too much of a Gump? It does not follow the trend of the Tide in their other three performances. Alabama has had a strong showing going over the Over/Under in all four affairs. Keelon Russell absolutely balled out on Saturday against South Carolina. If he can continue at that level of play against Mississippi State, there may be an exploding scoreboard in Starkville. The Bulldogs secondary is a bit on the sketchy side and the defense is prone to letdowns. For your consideration, this game will be played in Starkville with all those cowbells creating artificial noise. It will be much louder than Lexington was for the Crimson Tide in Week 2. The good side for Alabama is that they only have to travel about 90 minutes west to get to their destination. It's still six days away but the weather charts are calling for thunderstorms. Depending on how much wet stuff the field gets, there could be more dependencies on the running games by both teams. With an over/under of 59.5 and 4.5 point spread by FanDuel , the final score could look something like Bama 32-27. Are you buying that? I am expecting another big score. away.headline: Alabama starter ruled out for Mississippi State game
away.blurb: Alabama football has ruled out James for the Mississippi State game, per the SEC availability report Friday night. James was listed as questionable previously. James has been the Crimson Tide’s starting right tackle through the first four games. Alabama coach Kalen DeBoer noted he was on the practice field “a little bit” but was “very questionable” at the start of the week. The only other player on the availability report (who wasn’t already known to be previously out) is Zay Mincey, and the backup safety is probable to play against the Bulldo “Tyrell getting out there, he’s more than capable,” DeBoer said after the win over South Carolina . “He’s physically capable of getting it done. Happy that he got out there and had some success.” Jayvin James won’t get to face his former team. James left the South Carolina game in the second half with an injury. Tyrell Miller replaced him at right tackle for the rest of the game. James played for Mississippi State before he transferred to Alabama this offseason. That will leave defensive lineman Kedrick Bingley-Jones as the only Bulldogs transfer who will face his former team Saturday (11 a.m. CT, ABC). No. 7 Alabama will play No. 16 Mississippi State at Davis Wade Stadium in Starkville, Mississippi. The Bulldogs (4-0, 2-0 SEC) will look to beat the Crimson Tide (4-0, 2-0) for the first time since 2007. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit al.com. Distributed by Tribune Content Agency, LLC.

away.headline: Trump says he will attend Georgia-Alabama football game in Tuscaloosa
away.blurb: President Trump announced Friday that he will be returning to Alabama next week for the University of Georgia vs. University of Alabama college football game. He made the announcement while in Mobile, Ala. for a rally as part of his travels to several different states to rally Republicans ahead of the midterms. The game is set to take place on Saturday, Oct. 10 at 7:30 p.m. EDT at Bryant-Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa. The Georgia Bulldogs and Alabama Crimson Tide are currently ranked second and seventh, respectively, in this week's AP Top 25 . Trump attended the University of Texas vs. University of Tennessee college football game in Knoxville last week. It was the first game he attended since January’s College Football Playoff National Championship when Indiana University defeated the University of Miami. Trump has attended several sports events throughout his second term, including the FIFA World Cup finals in July and the Super Bowl in 2025. Earlier this month he attended the Irish Open at the Trump International Golf Links and Hotel in Doonbeg, Ireland. He also hosted a UFC fight on the South Lawn of the White House in June. But that's what Michigan is going to attempt to do this weekend after suffering a 20-19 loss to Iowa in Week 4. In reality, Michigan still holds its own fate in its hands . And that starts this weekend. The Wolverines hit the road for the first time and Michigan travels to take on Minnesota . The Gophers are coming off an impressive win over Washington, on the road, last weekend. Both programs enter Week 5 with a 3-1 record. Michigan is 78-25-3 all-time against Minnesota and this meeting will mark the 100th meeting for the Little Brown Jug. The Wolverines have won the last five games against Minnesota, but that doesn't mean Michigan can take this game for granted. Minnesota is a lot like Iowa. Neither program usually wows you on the offensive side of the ball, but defense and physicality can win them games. Minnesota hasn't quite lived up to expectations since P.J. Fleck was hired, but the Gophers haven't been an easy out when playing in Minnesota. Kyle Whittingham said this week that he feels like his team is 0-4, not 3-1. With a bye week coming up for Minnesota, this would be a great stepping stone to turning those feelings around and seeing Michigan play a complete game against a respectable opponent. picks.blurb: 3 Predictions for Michigan Football Against Minnesota Skip to main content SI.COM MORE SPORTS NEWS SI.COM WOLVERINES FB SI.COM WOLVERINES BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Michigan Wolverines will take on the Minnesota Golden Gophers on Saturday in their first road game of the season. The Wolverines are reeling coming off a 20-19 loss at home to the Iowa Hawkeyes, and need to bounce back before the schedule at the end of the season gets daunting. This is not your father’s Minnesota team. They are tough, resilient, and playing good football after last week’s 27-24 win over the Washington Huskies. PJ Fleck may be a little odd, but he has his team playing well. Will that be enough to spring an upset over the Wolverines who are favored on the road? Here are some of our predictions for Michigan’s first road game of the season. Jordan Marshall Goes for 100 Yards Jordan Marshall says he’s good to go. We’re taking him at his word here, but the Michigan run game needs to find some traction. The Wolverines have been putrid on the ground this season, and rank 92nd in the nation in yards-per-game . Michigan’s task did not get any easier this week, as Minnesota’s run defense has been stingy to start the year. This is the type of defense where run plays need to have yards come after the running back is first contacted. When he is healthy, that is Jordan Marshall’s specialty. He gives the Wolverines a personality in their run game, and is a violent runner. Last week, it looked like he was getting on track and running as hard as he has all season before curiously being out of the game for the final possession. Marshall is going to be the man, he’ll have some short runs earlier that turn into long runs as Michigan plays into the body-blow theory. The bet here also is that Marshall breaks a run for an explosive gain, which the Wolverines have not had on the ground for one of their running backs this season. Marshall tops the century mark for the first time for any Wolverine rusher this season. Michigan Defense Gets 3 Takeaways Where are the takeaways? Michigan’s defense has been great in almost every metric this season, but have been unable to take the ball away enough. The Wolverines had two takeaways against Oklahoma, and one against UTEP. That’s it so far this season, and their offense has been too sloppy with the ball. The result is that Michigan is currently minus-3 in the turnover margin. Yes, Michigan needs to play cleaner on offense, but their defense needs to start making some plays as well. MICHIGAN PICKS IT OFF! 🤯 #Michigan cornerback Jyaire Hill comes up with a clutch interception to put the Wolverines in the red zone! pic.twitter.com/QaalnVgmLD Drake Lindsey has a chance to be an NFL quarterback when his college career is over, but he has some arm arrogance to him. That’s a compliment, but also means he might put the ball in harm’s way. The bet this week is Michigan picks off two passes and gets a strip sack from someone we’re predicting as the star of the game. Tariq Boney is the Star of the Show Whether John Henry Daley plays or not, he’s likely to play on a reduced snap count thanks to a leg injury he suffered on the second-to-last play of last week’s game against Iowa. That will mean more snaps for the backup defensive ends. Tariq Boney has been productive whenever he has been on the field. He often reminds me of Chase Winovich during the 2016 season. Winovich did not play much on run downs, but was tasked with getting after the quarterback in obvious passing situations. That could be Boney’s role throughout the season, even if it’s not a perfect comparison between the two players. For the first time this season, Michigan hits the road and travels to Minnesota to take on the Gophers. Michigan has dominated this series and the Wolverines have won the last five meetings against Minnesota. But that doesn't mean the Gophers are going to lay down, and P.J. Fleck's team believes they have what it takes to upset the Wolverines. And so do some national analysts. We have predictions from three different sites, and then we determine if there is major concern for Michigan this weekend. The four-man crew at Fox Sports is leaning toward Minnesota. There were three members who took the Gophers, with one analyst taking Michigan. RJ Young - Minnesota Laken Litman - Minnesota Michael Cohen - Minnesota "Even though Michigan has a 3-1 overall record, it feels like there is an undercurrent of dysfunction for the Wolverines. Expect the Gophers to score a second consecutive upset. " Ben Portnoy - Michigan Both Brad Crawford and Chris Hummer believe Michigan will go into Minnesota and get the job done. Chris Hummer: Michigan 27-20 "The value in this game is with Minnesota. The Gophers are 3-1 with a quality road win over Washington. Meanwhile, the Wolverines have played four games this season, and three of them have been decided by seven points or fewer. But … I think Michigan has found something with Bryce Underwood. He's played much better the last two weeks -- a 68% completion rate, a four-to-one touchdown-to-interception ratio -- and Michigan is by far the best defense the Gophers have seen this season. The Wolverines respond on the road." Brad Crawford: Michigan 27-20 On3's J.D. PicKell The former Cornell and Baylor wide receiver has Michigan rowing the boat in Minnesota. "I think Michigan off a loss and that offense trending upward a little bit dangerous. I like it going to Minnesota. I love row the boat. Fun expression. The 107th meeting of one of college football's oldest rivalries is set for Saturday, Oct. 3, at noon ET on FOX, with Michigan and Minnesota squaring off at Huntington Bank Stadium in Minneapolis. The Wolverines are 5.5-point favorites, and my Michigan vs. Minnesota prediction and college football picks expect the maize and blue to retain the Little Brown Jug after winning the last six matchups. TOP PICK Who will win Michigan vs Minnesota: Michigan -5.5 The Michigan vs. Minnesota rivalry has been an ugly one for the Golden Gophers. Minnesota has won the Little Brown Jug just four times since 1968, while Michigan has taken it home on 44 different occasions (Michigan has covered in nine of the last 12 matchups). And though the Wolverines are coming off a tough loss to Iowa, I like them to cover -5.5 or better because of their defense. Michigan's stop unit ranks eighth in EPA per rush, 24th in EPA per pass, and 16th in available yards percentage (33.6%). Minnesota's inability to run the ball (103rd in EPA per rush) will put a lot on quarterback Drake Lindsey's plate, and his lack of mobility could be an issue against the Wolverines. Michigan's pass rush (assuming Dom Nichols and John Henry Daley play) is one of the best in the country, already boasting 12 sacks and 71 pressures . Michigan vs Minnesota Over/Under pick: Under 43.5 The Little Brown Jug game has hit the Over nine straight times, but Michigan's style of play should help break the trend, though I would only play the Under at 42.5 or better . The Wolverines have yet to score more than 19 points in a Power Four game this season, and they've yet to give up more than 20 points in any of their games, allowing just 14.8 ppg. Michigan has one of the best defenses in the country, ranked No. 9 by SP+ , but Minnesota has a pretty ferocious defense too. The Golden Gophers rank sixth nationally in havoc rate (23.7%) and should force QB Bryce Underwood into mistakes (his 5.4% turnover-worthy play rate is among the highest in the country). I predict the Wolverines to win 23-17. Michigan vs Minnesota combo Minnesota has long struggled to win the Little Brown Jug, and nothing has changed since Fleck took over. The Golden Gophers have kept the game within 20 points just once in the four matchups under Fleck. With both defenses ranking in the top 35 in net EPA per play, I'm expecting a slow, grind-it-out first half before Michigan pulls away late. Look for Wolverines wide receiver JJ Buchanan to be the X-factor. While this is Kyle Whittingham's first time in the rivalry, he's no stranger to winning rivalry games. As Utah's head coach, Whittingham went 11-6 in the Holy War against BYU. The Wolverines (3-1, 0-1 Big Ten) head on the road for the first time this season to face a 3-1 Minnesota team coming off an impressive road victory over Washington. Nevertheless, oddsmakers still view the Wolverines as a solid favorite. They have history on their side, too. The Wolverines have dominated the Little Brown Jug rivalry, winning 27 of the past 29 meetings and not losing in Minneapolis since 1977. Can they continue that success and bounce back in a big way? For Saturday's Big Ten clash between Michigan and Minnesota, the over/under is set at 43.5 total points on Polymarket . Michigan finds itself 3-1 but this feels like a second "bounce back" game. With a bye looming, the Wolverines desperately need a win in Minneapolis. The good news? Michigan is coming off a largely well-played game … the defense pitched a shutout through three quarters while the offense showed serious strides moving the football. I expect more of the same on Saturday against a Golden Gophers team that wants to be balanced and play it safe. I'm not expecting all will be cured, but I do expect Michigan to have more firepower and enough explosive plays to come away with a win. Michigan 24, Minnesota 17 After letting what looked like a sure win against Iowa slip away last week, expect the Wolverines to play a more complete game against a Minnesota team they hold a clear talent advantage over. The Gophers' front seven is legitimate, led by preseason Defensive Player of the Year Anthony Smith, so generating consistent production on the ground may not come easy. Still, I think Bryce Underwood builds on last week's performance and continues to lean on his two favorite targets, Andrew Marsh and JJ Buchanan. Look for Michigan to bottle up Minnesota's rushing attack and force Drake Lindsey into a few costly mistakes through the air. The Wolverines win the game and the turnover battle, bringing the Little Brown Jug back to Ann Arbor. Michigan 27, Minnesota 17 Michigan's offense should continue its upward trajectory Saturday and find the end zone a few times. The defense might have a little more trouble than last week: Lindsey is efficient if not explosive and Minnesota has a stable of capable running backs. Michigan has questions along the offensive line but still has Bryce Underwood, Andrew Marsh, and JJ Buchanan. They've played in harsh environments — Michigan visited Oklahoma, Nebraska, and Michigan State last season, winning twice — and shouldn't be intimidated by (checks notes) Huntington Bank Stadium. Michigan's win streak at Minnesota is remarkable. It predates P.J. Fleck's existence. Continuing that streak won't be easy. I expect Saturday's game to come down to the final minutes. Will it be decided on the final play , as two of Michigan's games have already? I guess we'll find out. Chengelis The Detroit News Oct. 2, 2026, 9:09 p.m. ET Hear this story View Comments MINNEAPOLIS -- Michigan right tackle Andrew Sprague and offensive lineman Manuel Biegel have been ruled out for the Wolverines ’ game at Minnesota on Saturday, Oct. 3. According to the Big Ten availability report issued Friday night, edge rushers John Henry Daley and Dom Nichols, receiver Andrew Marsh and offensive lineman Houston Ka’aha’aina-Torres remain listed as “questionable”, as has been the case since the first report Wednesday, Sept. 30. Sprague and Biegel were listed as “questionable” on the first two reports. Sprague has missed the last two games with an undisclosed injury and Biegel, used as a “rhino” or sixth lineman, missed the Iowa game last weekend. His injury also has not been publicly shared. Starting tackle Blake Frazier, who moved from left tackle to start at right tackle the last two games in place of Sprague, remains listed as “probable” for the Minnesota game. Frazier appeared to injure his right leg during Michigan’s second drive of the second half and after a brief visit to the medical tent, returned to the game. Offensive line coach Jim Harding said Wednesday he was hopeful Frazier will play. Nichols was listed as questionable the first three availability reports issued before the Iowa game but played in the Big Ten opener. Daley was injured on the second to last play of Michigan’s 20-19 loss to Iowa last Saturday, Sept. 26. Michigan (3-1, 0-1 Big Ten) faces Minnesota (3-1, 1-0) in the 100 th meeting for the Little Brown Jug, the oldest trophy game in college football. Marsh is coming off back-to-back 100-yard receiving games. He led Michigan with 10 catches for 105 yards and a touchdown against UTEP in Game 3, and against Iowa, he had 106 yards on seven catches.

away.headline: Mounting injuries take a toll on Michigan offensive line
away.blurb: The Wolverines have started three different line combinations so far, and may have to go with a fourth this Saturday at Minnesota (12 p.m. ET, FOX) if tackle Blake Frazier — injured in the loss to Iowa — has to sit out. Those changes haven’t helped continuity, an important part of building a reliable offensive line, Harding admitted. Evan Link began the season at left guard, missed Week 2 due to injury and returned against UTEP as the starting left tackle, forcing Frazier to the right side to fill in for the sidelined Andrew Sprague. With Sprague’s status in limbo, and tackle Andrew Babalola ruled out since camp, Michigan has been shorthanded in recent weeks up front. When Frazier left the game last weekend against Iowa, a true freshman, Marky Walbridge, had to replace him. The good news — if there is some — is that there may be some light at the end of the tunnel. Harding is hopeful that Frazier may be able to suit up and play this Saturday, while Babalola is expected to be cleared to return next week. If he is, Babalola would have a full two weeks to reintegrate — Michigan is on a bye next week — before making his debut. ANN ARBOR, Mich. — While injuries and reshuffling have slowed the Michigan offensive line through four games, coach Jim Harding isn’t making excuses. The veteran o-line coach has seen it all and knows that a successful offense depends on the group up front, which he classified as a work in progress on Wednesday. “Truthfully, it’s not where I want it to be and where I think it can be,” Harding told reporters. “And that falls on me ultimately. You could say, ‘well, you’ve had this many injuries’ or ‘this many missed games,’ and frankly nobody cares. There’s injuries all across the country. We’ve got to do a better job.” “I think our pass protection so far has been really good, especially comparing the same players to last year,” Harding said. “I think we can be more consistent in the run game, getting more push.” Harding did see some good things against Iowa, who Michigan ran for 153 yards against, but explosive runs have been few and far between. Through four games, Michigan is averaging just 4.03 yards per carry and is one of nine FBS teams with one run of 20-plus yards or fewer. “The line of scrimmage was moving this past week, so that’s progress,” Harding said. “But it’s nowhere near where it needs to be in my opinion, or it should be. As frustrated as maybe some people are, there’s not anyone more frustrated (than me).” And then there’s the mystery with Sprague, who was suddenly scratched from the starting lineup the Friday before the UTEP game. If and when he returns, the Michigan would be six deep and in a much better spot. The Wolverines were without a few major contributors along the offensive line last week against Iowa, and it’s still to be determined if some of them will be able to return this weekend, according to the initial Big Ten Conference injury report that was just released on Wednesday evening. After missing last week’s game, it’s good to see Beigel be upgraded to questionable. Elsewhere along the offensive line, Frazier is deemed probable to play this weekend after getting banged up last week. It’s still unclear what exactly is going on with Sprague, but he is listed as questionable once again. As for the defensive line, both of Michigan’s star edge rushers are listed as questionable after suffering respective injuries in the Iowa game.
