picks.headline: 3 Bold Predictions for the Iowa Hawkeyes vs Ohio State Buckeyes
picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions for the Iowa Hawkeyes vs Ohio State Buckeyes Skip to main content SI.COM SPRING SPORTS HAWKEYENATION SI.COM HAWKEYES FB SI.COM HAWKEYES BB BASKETBALL BASKETBALL NEWS MEN'S SCHEDULE MEN'S RANKINGS FOOTBALL NEWS Any time you are talking about a national title contender like Ohio State going down, you know it's going to take some bold plays and bold work from a team. If the Iowa Hawkeyes want to knock off Ohio State, things are going to have to break their way, but they also have to do their part in managing this game perfectly. It isn't just hoping to get the right bounce of the ball or be on the receiving end of a tipped pass like last week against Michigan. It requires some serious focus and attention, which is an area Iowa is an expert in. Kamari Moulton rushes for 100 yards Iowa knows it has to mitigate how many possessions Ohio State gets this week to stick around in this game and to keep the defense fresh. The Hawkeyes are going to give a heavy dose of running the ball to ensure that's the case. Kamari Moulton should be fresh after just 13 carries against Michigan last week. Expect Tim Lester and the offense to ask a lot of Moulton in this one. It may not be a consistent barrage of five yards on each touch. It is likely to be a case of banging into a brick wall for two and three yards at a time before Kamari Moulton pops a few chunk plays. Jeremiah Smith is held under 100 receiving yards Jeremiah Smith has been held under 100 yards just once this year. It wasn't by a bad game. Against Kent State, he had five receptions for 85 yards in a 59-3 win. It was to keep him healthy. His other games? He has had games of 151 yards, 164 yards, and 217 yards. He is doing whatever he wants, whenever he wants, against defenses. Phil Parker has been around the block once or twice before, and he has tried to contain stars before. Iowa is likely to throw the kitchen sink at Smith with double coverage, or safety help at the least, to force other Buckeyes' wide receivers to step up. Iowa forces at least 2 turnovers The Hawkeyes' defense knows they have to steal possessions in this game and create short fields for the offense. That's not meant as an indictment of the offense. Instead, it's a compliment to Ohio State. The Buckeyes are explosive, and taking the ball away from them is going to be key for Iowa this week. I expect Iowa to be hyper-aggressive in punching at the ball to force a fumble this week on each run play. If Iowa can steal a short field and translate that into three or seven points, with the clock running, that's a gigantic win for the Hawkeyes. Loading recommendations... On his Always College Football podcast , McElroy took the Buckeyes to win 24-14 on Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS. He said Iowa's defense will keep the game close for a half before wide receiver Jeremiah Smith takes over. "Kinnick will be rocking," McElroy said. "I just don't know if Iowa has the downfield passing attack to punish a defense that's going to be squatting all game long on the run game." McElroy ranked Ohio State No. 1 in his preseason top 10 in August. The Buckeyes have since lost 24-23 at Texas, but they're 1-0 in Big Ten play, the same as the unbeaten Hawkeyes. Why did McElroy pick Ohio State? picks.blurb: David Pollack Picks Winner of Ohio State-Iowa Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS The biggest game of the week in the Big Ten is No. 14-ranked Iowa hosting No. 5 Ohio State in Iowa City on Saturday. The Hawkeyes are traditionally tough to beat at home in Kinnick Stadium, but the Buckeyes are 17-3 all-time in the series and 6-1 vs. Iowa over the last 20 years with the lone loss in that span coming in Iowa City in 2017. Kickoff is set for 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS with Ohio State (3-1, 1-0 Big Ten) set as a 14-point road favorite over Iowa (4-0, 1-0), per DraftKings Sportsbook . College football analyst David Pollack broke down the matchup on his "See Ball Get Ball" podcast. Alabama-Mississippi State, Ohio State-Iowa, Florida-Missouri AND MORE Week 5 CFB Picks https://t.co/8vWS9mTHpm "I think [Iowa] has a chance because Ohio State's defense is more gettable than they've been, but to me that means Iowa has to have some passing game, a little bit of balance, run it more than they've run it, have success and defensively hold the heck on. Like just hold on, don't give up big plays, make them get in the red zone and kick 3s," Pollack said. David Pollack Makes His Pick for Ohio State-Iowa In dissecting the matchup, Pollack focused on two key components. First, he hasn't been impressed by Ohio State's defense, which lost most of its starters from last season, including three of the top 11 picks in the NFL draft. But Pollack also doesn't know how much he trusts Iowa's offense and quarterback Hank Brown to take advantage of that. "I watched every snap of Ohio State vs. Illinois. I thought [the Buckeyes'] defense, I think they've got some guys who flash occasionally, but they gave up over 6 yards a carry to Illinois. To give up almost 200 yards rushing, this is what Iowa is, this is who they want to be -- they want to run the football," Pollack said. "... Hank Brown, he needs to make a few plays down the field. They need to be able to open it up a little bit because I know they're going to run it, and I think they can run it at a decent clip." Iowa ranks 27th nationally in rushing at 215.5 yards per game, led by Kamari Moulton (284 yards and 2 TDs on 7.3 yards per carry) with a few other running backs all contributing in significant ways. But the Hawkeyes rank just 87th in passing at 213.5 YPG while Brown has thrown for 700 yards, 5 TDs and 0 INTs. Iowa's strength, as always, is its defense, which has given up the fewest points in college football (8.0 per game) while ranking 10th at the FBS level overall (239.8 YPG). The Hawkeyes haven't yet played an offense like Ohio State's, however, shutting out Northern Illinois and Northern Iowa while containing limited offenses from Iowa State and Michigan. The Buckeyes are led by two Heisman Trophy candidates in 2025 finalist Julian Sayin (1,206 passing yards, 12 TDs and 1 INT) and star wideout Jeremiah Smith (33 catches for an FBS-leading 617 yards and 7 TDs). In Ohio State's Big Ten opener vs. Illinois last week, a 42-19 win, Smith had 12 catches for 217 yards and 4 TDs. Jeremiah Smith just settled ALL DEBATES, he is the GREATEST WR prospect ever. • 12 receptions (career-high) • 217 receiving yards (career-high) • 4 receiving TD’s (career-high) The Buckeyes WR was UNSTOPPABLE in the GREATEST game of his career 🤯🍿 pic.twitter.com/DhJLDREfJc But Pollack wonders if the Buckeyes' lacking rushing attack (156.75 YPG, 76th nationally) is their vulnerability in a matchup like this. "With Ohio State on the other side, man, is it anybody besides Jeremiah Smith? And here's the thing with Ohio State, can they get that run game going? ... At some point in this season they're going to need to get first downs and punch it in the red zone," Pollack said. As for his ultimate prediction for the matchup, Pollack is taking the Buckeyes and sticking close to the spread set by the oddsmakers. "I think this is a phenomenal matchup. I think Iowa is going to keep it close," he said. "If you weren't watching last week, Illinois kept it close. Illinois was very much in the game until the very last little bit, but they were still very much in striking distance. I think this is 27-13 type of a deal. "I don't think Iowa's offense is good enough. ... It's all about the offense because I think they can hang on long enough, make them kick a few field goals to stay in the game, but the [arrow points toward] Jeremiah Smith and Julian Sayin." Happy prediction Friday, Hawkeye fans! Tomorrow is the day you've all been waiting for for some time - a colossal matchup at Kinnick Stadium between No. 14 Iowa and No. 5 Ohio State on Saturday (2:30 p.m. CT, CBS). After careful consideration, here's how I see this battle playing out. Where/When To Watch Matchup: No. 5 Ohio State (3-1, 1-0) @ No. 14 Iowa (4-0, 1-0) Scheduled game time: Oct. 3 at 2:30 p.m. CT Location: Kinnick Stadium in Iowa City, Iowa Weather: 68 degrees Announcers: Brad Nessler (play-by-play), Charles Davis (analyst), Jenny Dell (sideline) Radio: Hawkeye Radio Network (Gary Dolphin, Pat Angerer) Student Radio: KRUI (Collin Carrithers, Cole Krueger) Before we talk about the actual football game, let's begin this pick by talking about the electric atmosphere we're about to witness inside Kinnick Stadium on Saturday. This is easily Iowa's biggest home game at least in five years (No. 3 Iowa vs. No. 4 Penn State in 2021), and you probably have to go all the way back to the 2006 showdown between the Hawkeyes and Buckeyes to find a more important game in Iowa City. Iowa fans have waited for this game since the schedule came out in February, and the buzz in this city is palpable right now. College GameDay returning for the first time in 20 years has only increased it. The crowd might be the only advantage Iowa has on the gridiron, though. Though it blew a 20-point fourth quarter lead at Texas a few weeks ago, Ohio State still might be the most-talented team in the nation. The Hawkeyes are going to have their hands full against the Buckeyes, but the one thing Iowa will always have? Heart. That competitive grit was evident in the thrilling comeback victory over Michigan last weekend, and the Hawkeyes will certainly need it to keep pace with an explosive Buckeye offense. Speaking of offense, how will Iowa stop Jeremiah Smith? Smith is not only the best wide receiver in the country, he may just be the best player in the entire sport. Not only is he fast and an excellent route runner, his 6-foot-4, 222-pound frame makes him a dangerous threat in 50/50, red zone situations. Smith is likely going to make a few big plays in this game, but what concerns me the most is Iowa trying to get pressure on Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin. The Hawkeyes are never going to be a blitz-first team under Phil Parker, but have you seen how accurate Sayin is? He's not much of a running threat, but Iowa has to get pressure on him if it wants to stay in this ballgame. I think the Hawkeyes will get to Sayin a few times, but I don't think it's going to be enough. Iowa is going to cover the spread and move the ball against a shaky Ohio State defensive front , but the Buckeyes just make a few more big plays to pull away for a victory. The ESPN host sees running back Jadan Baugh and the Gators' ground game as the biggest problem for a Tigers team that just lost its conference opener. On his Always College Football podcast , McElroy picked Florida to win 31-24 on Saturday, Oct. 3, at 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC. "Florida has a deeper offense," he said, "and Missouri's red zone issues, that's something that's difficult to overcome in this game." Florida jumped from No. 21 to No. 8 in the Top 25 poll after a 52-28 win over No. 4 Ole Miss. Missouri slid from No. 19 to No. 25 after it gave up the last 14 points in a 31-24 loss at Mississippi State. "So, for Missouri, this is got-to-have-it mode, given what's coming up here in the next few weeks," McElroy said. McElroy has liked this Florida team since the summer , when he said the Gators could play spoiler in the 2026 Playoff race. How can Missouri slow Jadan Baugh? The program is off to its best start since 2019, but there is potential for an upset on Saturday . Ahead of the SEC showdown inside Memorial Stadium, CBS Sports writers Brad Crawford and Chris Hummer offer their predictions and picks for one of Week 5's best offerings. Both agree that Jon Sumrall and Co. will prevail, but they also concur that it will be a close one, taking the under on the 4.5-point spread. "Here's the Week 5 line that provided immediate pause when putting this week's card together — something ain't right here," Crawford begins. "Florida just rushed for 302 yards against Ole Miss and looks the part under first-year coach Jon Sumrall, while the Tigers are licking their road-woe wounds following a loss at Mississippi State. Winning away from home in the SEC is hard, and the Gators are going to get all they can handle according to oddsmakers." Crawford picks Florida to emerge triumphant from the gridiron grind, 31-27. Hummer, on the other hand, sees this finishing by a razor-thin margin. "This is probably the toughest test for Florida's offense so far this year," he notes. "The Tigers rank 19th nationally in yards allowed per carry and can at least limit Jadan Baugh. They also have a pass rush that can speed up Aaron Philo in obvious pass situations. Missouri does really miss Ahmad Hardy, ranking just 89th nationally in rushing yards per carry. But Austin Simmons has been excellent since transferring in from Ole Miss. Florida is a justified road favorite. But I think Missouri keeps this close enough to cover at home." Hummer predicts a narrow one-point victory, with a final score of 35-34 . The battle between Florida and Missouri is set to kick off at 3:30 p.m. ET on Saturday at Faurot Field and will be broadcast on ABC. picks.blurb: David Pollack Picks Winner of Florida-Missouri - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus 49ers owner suspended, fined WNBA playoffs CBS, Tony Romo part ways Browns outlast Steelers Duren, Pistons reach deal David Pollack Picks Winner of Florida-Missouri Running back Jadan Baugh has led No. 8-ranked Florida to a 4-0 record and mounting national buzz as the Gators take on No. 25 Missouri. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ryan Young Fri, October 2, 2026 at 8:38 PM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads A week ago, Florida was the team in prime position to deliver an upset while playing at home against an opponent, Ole Miss, that was coming off a huge win the previous week. The role is reversed in Week 5 for the No. 8-ranked Gators (4-0, 2-0 SEC), who delivered their statement with a 52-28 win over that then-top-5 Rebels team and now must avoid a letdown of their own on the road against No. 25 Missouri (3-1, 0-1). Florida is set as a 5.5-point road favorite, per DraftKings Sportsbook , in a matchup that kicks off at 3:30 p.m. ET Saturday on ABC. College football analyst David Pollack dissected the matchup on his "See Ball Get Ball" podcast. "I want to be Missouri so bad in this matchup because everybody, everybody is like 'Oh, this Buster Faulkner guy's good. This Jon Sumrall guy's good!'" Pollack said of Florida's much ballyhooed new offensive coordinator and head coach. "We've been talking about it for a while -- welcome aboard everybody. "Here's the thing why this matchup becomes really awesome. You have that going for you, again, just like [with Florida vs. Ole Miss] last week, Missouri is playing at home. Florida is not sneaking up on anybody, right?" David Pollack Makes His Prediction For Florida-Missouri Pollack explained why he believes Missouri can potentially be a tough matchup for the Gators and what the Tigers are going to need to do to pull the upset. To put it simply, that requires slowing down running backs Jadan Baugh (600 rushing yards and 11 TDs on 7.2 yards per carry) and Duke Clark (259 yards and 3 TDs on 8.1 YPC) and a Florida rushing attack that ranks 11th nationally at 260.0 YPG while forcing quarterback Aaron Philo to make more plays with his arm. Philo, the Georgia Tech transfer who followed Faulker to Florida and is in his first season as a starter, has only attempted 87 passes in four games for 917 yards, 7 TDs and 2 INTs. Philo was 16-of-23 passing for 196 yards, 1 TD and 0 INTs plus a rushing TD in the win over Ole Miss. "Missouri's defense, watching them vs. Mississippi State, Missouri's defense always finds a way to be physical, they always find a way to be good in the front 7. They can rush the passer, 10 coming off the edge is consistently a problem," Pollack said of edge rusher Daeden Hopkins, who has 6 sacks and 2 forced fumbles already. "... Here's what I'm interested to see, this is the only thing that matters to me, can you put it in Philo's hands? Like literally, at some point who can make Philo be a QB because right now -- and I'm not knocking Philo, they're doing what they need to do and they're undefeated -- but right now Philo is getting worn out by handing that thing off. "Over 300 [rushing yards] a game the last two games against Auburn and Ole Miss. That is a feat, that is impressive. The offensive line is impressive. The system is impressive. Who is going to be the first to say, 'Philo, you've got to beat me'? And can he go through progressions and make those plays when it's not the easy stuff. Can you take away the layups, get him off schedule a little bit? If Missouri can do that at home, that will be interesting for me to watch. That's what I'm looking for the most in this game." Missouri lost its SEC opener 31-24 at Mississippi State last week and has played only one other Power 4 teams so far (a 38-21 win at Kansas). The Tigers are led by quarterback Austin Simmons, the Ole Miss transfer who has passed for 947 yards, 11 TDs and 0 INTs so far. Jamal Roberts (395 rushing yards and 3 TDs on 4.4 YPC) leads the rushing attack, that is still waiting for star Ahmad Hardy to return as he continues to recover and work back from an offseason gunshot wound. Ultimately, Pollack is picking the Gators to win by a comfortable margin. He's a believer in what Sumrall has built in his first season at Florida. "I trust Florida by this point now, I do. I trust them," Pollack said. "I will say this, Florida's receiving corps is banged up to heck. It's going to be very interesting to watch them. I've got Florida 38, Missouri 27ish. I'm trusting Florida on the road after a big game." Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. away.blurb: News Sports Opinion Guardian Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL Florida football injury update: VBIII, Bailey Stockton questionable for Mizzou Kevin Brockway Gainesville Sun Updated Sept. 30, 2026, 8:53 p.m. ET Florida football wide receivers Vernell Brown III and Bailey Stockton have been listed as questionable for UF's game at No. 25 Missouri (October 3, 3:30 p.m., ABC) on the SEC's Initial Availability Report released on September 30. Brown III suffered a knee injury after an 11-yard run in the second quarter during UF's 52-28 win over Ole Miss and did not return. Stockton, meanwhile, suffered a back injury on a helmet-to-helmet targeting hit by Ole Miss safety Joenel Arguero, who was ejected on the play. He returned to field punts in the second half but has been limited in practice this week. If Stockton and Brown are both out, Florida could turn to receivers Eric Singleton Jr., Kahleil Jackson and Micah Mays Jr. for more snaps against Missouri. Singleton returned to the field after sitting out two-plus game with an ankle injury and caught a 38-yard pass against Ole Miss, while also forcing a pass interference penalty. Missouri running back Ahmad Hardy, the SEC's leading rusher from 2025 with 1,649 yards, remains out while recovering from a gunshot wound in his leg. Also out for the Tigers (3-1, 0-1 SEC) are safety, JaDon Blair, running back Malae Fonoti, offensive lineman Josh Atkins and tight end Gavin Hoffman. Edge rushers Langden Kitchen and Darris Smith and linebacker Bobby Washington Jr. are questionable for Missouri. Brown leads the No. 8 Florida Gators (4-0, 2-0 SEC) in receiving with 17 catches for 271 yards and 2 TDs. He's also been a weapon on special teams with two punt returns for TDs. Stockton, meanwhile, has 13 catches for 106 yards and 1 TD on the season. Florida football may need to turn to depth at WR "He played 8-9 snaps," said Florida football offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner, who coached Singleton at Georgia Tech. "He went deep three or four; he got a pass interference; he got the 38-yard gain. So, yeah, he brings a totally different element when it comes to being able to take the top off of defense than really anybody I've ever been around." UF has been relatively healthy so far under first-year coach Jon Sumrall, in part due to a strength and conditioning program under Rusty Whitt that focuses on building strength for injury prevention. Whitt is having players maintain a strict weight room schedule during the regular season. "We've put a lot of work in," Sumrall said. "You know, things that are strong are resilient and don't break easily. So there's a lot of work that's been put in by Rusty (Whitt) and Paul Silvestri and that group. Very grateful for our sports medicine team and strength staff, they all do a phenomenal job." Kevin Brockway is The Gainesville Sun’s Florida beat writer. Contact him at kbrockway@gannett.com. Follow him on X @KevinBrockwayG1.

away.blurb: Three Gators will be limited in practice during Week 5 after suffering injuries in Florida's 52-28 win over Ole Miss. Gators head coach Jon Sumrall detailed No. 8 Florida's injury report on Monday ahead of its Week 5 matchup at No. 25 Missouri, noting wide receivers Vernell Brown III (knee), Bailey Stockton (back) and cornerback Dijon Johnson (ankle) will be limited in practice throughout the week and that "all of them, honestly, could be available this weekend." Brown exited Florida's 52-28 win over Ole Miss Saturday with a slight limp after a six-yard reverse rush in the second quarter and did not return, although his run converted a first down six plays before Florida running back Jadan Baugh scored his second touchdown of the contest, giving UF a 17-3 lead. "Bailey Stockton will be limited probably a good bit of the week, just because of, he like, basically a car crash on the field with two guys," Sumrall said. "Came back and fought through it. You know, back's a little bit sore, but it's nothing structurally wrong, and so, working through that." "None of those injuries are long-term, catastrophic; all of them, honestly, could be available this weekend," said Sumrall. "That'll just be through the week evaluations. But I've had guys -- on all the guys who have injuries -- I've had guys have the same injuries and find ways to get there in a week, but you never know how a guy's body is going to respond and how they feel confidence-wise and certain things. home.blurb: Two injured Missouri football defensive ends questionable for Florida game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Two injured Missouri football defensive ends questionable for Florida game Mizzou coach Eli Drinkwitz said Tuesday, Sept. 29 that injured edge rushers Darris Smith and Langden Kitchen are both questionable for the Tigers ' game against Florida . The No. 25-ranked Tigers will play No. 8 Florida, which currently ranks No. 5 in the FBS with 532.8 yards of total offense per game, on Saturday in Columbia. Smith and Kitchen were Mizzou's starting defensive ends in each of their first three games of the season, but over the past two game weeks, both players have left the field with injuries and were unable to return. Smith was helped off the field during the first half of Mizzou's Week 3 win over Troy due to an ankle injury. He attempted to return in the second half but only remained on the field for one play. The fifth-year senior did not play in MU's loss at Mississippi State this past Saturday. Kitchen came off the field during the first quarter of the game against the Bulldogs and was evaluated for a lower-body injury. He did not return to the field. "Both are doing the very best they can to get back," Drinkwitz said. "I doubt they can participate in much of any practice today (Tuesday), but both of those guys are experienced. You know, our protocol is you have to practice by Thursday in order to be available for the game. Life in the SEC, that's kind of how we go about it with guys who are questionable." The possible designations, from most likely to play to least likely, are as follows: available; probable; questionable; doubtful; out. picks.blurb: Staff predictions for Virginia vs Florida State — a high-end rematch on deck Skip to main content SI.COM MEN'S BASKETBALL WOMEN'S BASKETBALL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM CAVALIERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM CAVALIERS BB To keep pace and maintain a tie for first place in the ACC, Virginia must conquer Florida State in its first true road game of 2026. An ACC road game is never easy — but the Cavaliers are actually favored to pick up a win at the feared Doak Campbell Stadium. Here are game predictions from the Virginia On SI staff: Jackson Caudell: Virginia 31, Florida State 21 I think this is going to be an interesting test for UVA. While FSU and West Virginia are not the same team, they pose similar challenges. The Seminoles are a mess, but they have talented running backs and a quarterback who can stress you with his legs, much like WVU. Playing away from Charlottesville has not been kind to Virginia so far this year (though a small sample size), and I think they need to be careful here. Most everyone is overlooking Florida State, but they can win this game. However, I have far more trust in Tony Elliott to go on the road and get a win to remain unbeaten in ACC play. Xander Tilock: Virginia 38, Florida State 27 At first glance, I was leaning towards picking the Seminoles at home. However, there are two major factors that make it essentially impossible for Florida State to win. The Seminoles have the ACC's second-worst pass defense through four games — so Virginia should have little trouble scoring 35-plus points. However, the other side of the ball is more important, particularly because Florida State has turned the ball over at an average greater than once per game. The Cavaliers can capitalize on those turnovers by turning them into lengthy touchdown drives. Florida State is capable of making things interesting — especially at home — but there are a few reasons why Virginia is the favorite in an ACC road game. This should be a Cavaliers win by multiple scores. Steve DeShazo: Virginia 27, Florida State 31 Saturday brings Virginia's first true road game of 2026. It comes against a proud and talented team that has not played up to its capabilities and may be competing to save Coach Mike Norvell's job in the same way I believe the Cavaliers did for Elliott last year. FSU's offensive skill trio of quarterback Ashton Daniels, receiver Ousman Kromah and receiver Duce Robinson will be a handful for the Cavaliers to contain. Beau Pribula could have a field day passing against the Seminoles, and it may be mandatory to keep Virginia close. The Cavaliers have yet to win a close game or pull out a victory away from home this season. picks.headline: Staff Predictions: Florida State Seminoles vs. Virginia Cavaliers
picks.blurb: Predictions: Florida State Seminoles vs. Virginia | Tomahawk Nation Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Florida State Seminoles Community Tomahawk Nation October 3, 2026 Tomahawk Nation Notifications Notifications The Feed Betting FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Florida State Football Odds Florida State Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Florida State Football FSU looking to get to .500 in ACC action for first time since 2023 Florida State hosts the Virginia Cavaliers for the first time since 2014, a 34-20 Seminole win, on Saturday at Doak Campbell Stadium in Tallahassee. Kickoff is scheduled for 3:30 p.m., and the game will be televised on ESPN2. Of the 21 meetings between FSU and UVA, Saturday marks only the third time (2006, 2010, 2026) that neither team is ranked in the Associated Press Top 25. Florida State (2-2, 0-1 ACC) and the Cavaliers (3-1, 1-0 ACC) will meet for the second straight season and the 21st time overall in UVA’s first true road game of the ‘26 season. FSU and UVA have not met in back-to-back seasons since the 2010 and 2011 seasons, with FSU holding a 15-5 all-time record against UVA, including a 9-1 record at Doak. Virginia’s only victory came in 2011 when the Wahoos defeated the then-No. 23 Seminoles, 14-13. UVA will be trying for its third consecutive win and fourth in its last five meetings with the Noles. Saturday will be a rematch of last year’s double-overtime loss by then-No. 8 FSU in Charlottesville, which ended with a game-sealing interception in the end zone by the Cavaliers. The victory was UVA’s first over a top-10 opponent at home since defeating then-No. 4 Florida State 26-21 in 2005. Virginia’s defense comes into the contest allowing just 130 passing yards per game, the fifth-fewest in the nation and the lowest in the ACC, and ranked 14th in total defense, giving up just 247 yards per game. Opposing quarterbacks sport an 84.2 efficiency rating, the lowest in the country. UVA is one of 20 FBS teams allowing fewer than 14 points per game. The Cavaliers have held two of its four opponents without a touchdown and only allowed a total of 52 points on the season. On offense, UVA quarterback Beau Pribula ranks fifth nationally in passing efficiency (194.1), with 11 touchdown passes, tying for seventh in the country, and tied for fourth in the ACC. Eighteen Cavaliers have caught a pass this season, and each of UVA’s last three games has featured double-digit pass catchers. Pribula has completed 66 of 86 passes and ranks fourth in the nation with a 77% completion percentage. The Seminoles are coming off their second win of the season after unimpressively beating outmanned Central Arkansas, 34-7. The Noles went 4-for-4 in the Red Zone against Central Arkansas and are now 17-for-17 to begin the 2026 season. FSU’s 17 Red Zone conversions are the 4th most in the country among the 19 teams that are still perfect inside the 20. Jayvan Boggs, Seminoles coast past Central Arkansas to get back to .500 FSU QB Ashton Daniels is 58-of-97 passing for 928 yards and six touchdowns, with 142 rushing yards and four rushing touchdowns. He has accounted for multiple touchdowns in all four games. Daniels is the only player in FBS in 2026 with multiple rushing and passing touchdowns and a two-point conversion. On the season, the Noles’ offense is ranked a not-so-nice 69th in total offense, 76th in the nation in 3rd down conversions with just a 40.8% rate on 20-of-49 attempts, and tied for 63rd in scoring offense with a 32-point average per game. FSU’s 126th-ranked total defense is allowing 430 total yards per game, 290 passing yards per game (135th out of 138 FBS teams), and ranked 121st in third-down percentage, allowing opponents to convert almost 46% of the time on third-down attempts. 2026 FSU Schedule Preview: Virginia Cavaliers Florida State is trending as a 2.5-point underdog, with the over/under set at 51.5 points according to FanDuel. Read what your TOMAHAWK NATION PROGNOSTICATORS think about this Saturday’s showdown. Then look over and digest all the FREE PRE-GAME CONTENT we’ve posted leading up to this game. We would love to hear your thoughts about how you feel about this game and your final score prediction in the comments. Curt Weiler (season record: 4-0, 2-2 ATS) Considering FSU’s defensive problems against talented teams this season, it’s hard to predict the success will begin against a Virginia offense, which has thrown 15 touchdowns to one interception this season while rushing for nearly 200 yards per game. And that doesn’t even factor in a Virginia defense which is second in the ACC in yards per play allowed (4.1) on a team that has a plus-five turnover differential this season. FSU will need its home-field advantage to work overtime to make up for what feels like a talent discrepancy, as wild as that is to say considering Virginia has won at Doak Campbell Stadium exactly one time. Virginia 31, Florida State 24 Matt Minnick (season record: 4-0, 3-1 ATS) This game is FSU’s season. A win on Saturday and the ‘Noles move to 1-1 in ACC play and a chance to really establish some momentum the following week with a suddenly vulnerable Louisville squad. Lose to UVA, and it becomes hard to see Florida State avoiding a tailspin that results in a 3-9 type season. When you look at the advanced stats, Florida State’s offense is respectable in many areas. It’s still a small sample size, but adjusted for SOS, the ‘Noles have the 18th best offense overall according to FEI, better than Nebraska, Texas, UCLA, LSU, SMU, Louisville, Virginia Tech, UVA, and a host of other teams with better records. Buoying the FSU offense are their explosive plays, ranking 36th in points per drive and 38th in yards per play. However, there is one area FSU’s offense really struggles in, and that is “busted drive rate” where the ‘Noles rank 90th. A “busted drive” is defined as a drive that gains 0 or fewer net yards, and here in lies Florida State’s biggest problem. FSU’s boom and bust offense does a nice job of putting points on the board in bunches, but when you have a defense that cannot get off the field (even when playing inferior opponents), it is essential that you consistently sustain success on offense. Otherwise, every busted drive results in your opponent receiving better and better field position and chewing up more and more of the clock. Not playing complementary football has been a theme under Norvell, and thus far this season is no exception. Virginia’s defense admittedly has not faced a murderer’s row, but they rank 13th in defensive busted drive rate. If the busted drive trends for both teams hold, it’s hard to see Florida State emerging victorious. But if FSU can find a way to limit their three and outs and turnovers, the Seminoles might be able to hit enough explosives to outscore the ‘Hoos at home. For the second time this season, FSU finds itself a short underdog at home, a typical “sharp spot” for betters in Vegas. Similar to the SMU game, I think FSU has its chances but just can’t quite find a way to get the W. UVA 35, FSU 34 Jordan Silversmith (season record: 4-0) Last year’s loss to Virginia turned Florida State’s season sideways at a pivotal moment. Saturday will do the same thing. UVA is favored by Vegas — on the road — because they are the better team. The Cavs are the most experienced squad in the country and have an identity on both sides of the ball. Meanwhile, Florida State is still finding itself. On offense, they are boom-or-bust, producing explosive plays on the ground and through the air but unable to sustain drives. Defensively, FSU’s defensive coordinator Tony White apologized to the offense after the Central Arkansas game for letting the Bears hold the ball for 40 minutes of time of possession. That says all that anyone needs to know about where the Seminoles are on that side of the ball. Even if FSU technically has better players, as Virginia is ranked 57th in 247Sports’ Talent Composite, UVA has the better, coach, quarterback, and knows how to win. Virginia wins and covers. UVA 31, FSU 27 NoleThruandThru (season record: 4-0) I’m just here so I don’t get fined. FSU 31, Virginia 28 LastNoleOfKrypton (season record: 3-0) All week I’ve been setting up how this is a bad match-up for FSU and how the more experienced, better coach, better quarterback, and better match-up UVA team should win, so naturally I’m going with the ‘Noles. Boom or bust offenses work better at home than on the road, and this is UVA’s first true road test of the year, as their only game away from the comforts of Charlottesville so far was a neutral-site loss to West Virginia. FSU 28, UVA 27 Jon Marchant (season record: 2-0 ) Virginia’s Beau Pribula is very good at keeping Virginia ahead of the chains, whether it’s with quick passes or his legs. However, if you can get Virginia into obvious passing downs, that’s where he struggles. Meanwhile, the Seminoles’ offense is very boom or bust—if they hit an explosive play, they have a chance to score. away.headline: Virginia's lengthy injury report gives Florida State an obvious Week 5 game plan
away.blurb: The Seminoles essentially have to win this weekend versus the Virginia Cavaliers to get their season back on track. Mike Norvell is coaching for his job, and the only real way to do that is by essentially winning out in ACC play. This is an extremely daunting task, but the only way to eat an elephant is by taking it one bite at a time, and that is exactly what the game will be. Now that the injury reports have gone up for the matchup , it is easier to determine how this game will look. While both teams have a number of key players out, the focus for Florida State fans should be on the losses for Virginia on their defensive line. The biggest name to look for in that area is defensive tackle Jason Hammond. Hammond entered the season as one of the players with the most hype on the Virginia defensive front. This was supposed to be the year when Hammond finally took those next steps and solidified himself as one of the better linemen in the conference, but now it appears his return this season is in question. Kromah appears poised to remain the bell cow and should mostly see the opposing starters, but Wisner is where the lack of depth for Virginia will start to show itself. As the Cavaliers start to sub players out, FSU will try to spell Kromah with the equally-capable Wisner, and that is where FSU will need to force their will on a depleted opponent. The Wisner hype was perhaps a little too premature coming into the season based on his limited reps leading up to last week, but he has an easy path towards showing why the Seminoles put so much faith in him with a nice chunk of money on the transfer market. Virginia's lengthy injury report gives Florida State an obvious Week 5 game plan Skip to main content Recruiting In the world of college football, teams will take whatever they can get if that gives them a chance to win. This is especially the case for a team like Florida State. Hammond absolutely leaves a hole on defense for the Cavaliers and his loss is further felt by the loss of depth across the front. Devon Baxter is the next most notable name to miss this weekend, largely a backup on the season, but several other depth players are also missing, leaving the Virginia rush defense susceptible. The good news for FSU is that their rushing attack is one of their biggest strengths, and Ousmane Kromah and Tre Wisner are more than up to the task . This game will still probably have some uphill sledding for the Noles to overcome, but this does at least display the obvious path for an FSU win and earn its first ACC win of the season. home.blurb: Florida State linebacker Noah LaVallee was downgraded from probable to out after there was previously hope he would play in Week 5. The Seminoles will be without four linebackers after the LaVallee announcement, as the freshman will join Izayia Williams, Blake Nichelson, and Daylen Green on the sidelines this week. Noah's brother and fellow linebacker, Caleb, is currently listed as probable for the upcoming game. Florida State's linebacker depth just took another hit with Noah LaVallee downgraded to out for Week 5 Florida State entered the game with a handful of players already confirmed to be out of the Week 5 game, but losing LaVallee particularly stings since he is a player filling in due to the injuries. LaVallee did not record any stats through the first three games, but began to work into the rotation against Central Arkansas with 21 snaps. The injury list is still rather long, even with a handful of players removed. Defensive back Quindarrius Jones and Caleb LaVallee are still listed as probable for the upcoming game against Virginia. Florida State and Virginia both released lengthy injury reports ahead of the Week 5 battle on Saturday. Both teams will be without a good chunk of the roster, but the key difference is that the Seminoles will be without multiple players at a vital position, and another player from the same position just joined that list. 2026 has not been the most productive season up to this point for Florida State, with a handful of players powering through bumps and bruises to compensate for the number of more serious injuries, particularly on defense. Starting safety Ashlynd Barker has been playing through a broken bone in his arm, although somewhat controversially , to make up for the shocking injury total. Without Noah and potentially Caleb in the picture, the slack will need to be picked up by the likes of Karon Maycock and AJ Cottrill. Maycock, a freshman, saw his first real action of the season against Central Arkansas and recorded three total tackles. Cottrill, on the other hand, saw action against SMU and Central Arkansas, totaling two tackles. During the Week 3 game against Alabama in Tuscaloosa, Florida State only played four linebackers and opted to use plenty of defensive backs. With Mikai Gbayor, Chris Jones, and Omar Graham Jr. all expected to play in Week 5, the Seminoles' staff might just give the remaining snaps at linebacker to the more experienced Cottrill. The only issue, however, is that Alabama and Virginia are far different teams in terms of how the offense attacks opposing defenses. Virginia is going to look to keep the football on the ground for most of the game. When combined with the play-action heavy passing attack, the Seminoles' linebackers could tire easily, which will force more of the remaining depth into the game. picks.blurb: South Carolina vs Kentucky Predictions: Will the Gamecocks End an Ugly SEC Losing Streak This Weekend? Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM GAMECOCKS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM GAMECOCKS BB This may be one of the most important games of the Shane Beamer era on Saturday. The season is on the verge of running off the tracks and the result of this game could smooth things out for another week or completely derail the entire season. Who comes out on top in a battle between former SEC East foes? South Carolina is in the midst of an eight game losing streak to Power Four opponents, which includes seven losses to SEC teams. During this losing streak Beamer's Gamecocks have fallen to Alabama (twice), LSU, Oklahoma, Mississippi State, Texas A&M, and Ole Miss. Their last win came against Kentucky in a 35-13 route of the Wildcats. However now with Will Stein at the helm, this is not the same Kentucky team of recent years. Wildcats QB Kenny Minchey and this offense have been very efficient and moved the ball well. They got a statement win earlier in the year at College Station and are looking for another. What may help South Carolina in this one is Kentucky's leaky defense . The Wildcats rank 14th in scoring (25 ppg), 12th in rushing (122.25 yards per game), and 13th against the pass (234 yards per game). Rain may be in the forecast for this weekend. This very well could play right into the Gamecocks' hands as they have a much improved rushing attack from last season. picks.blurb: Kentucky at South Carolina: Final Thoughts and Prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus 49ers owner suspended, fined WNBA playoffs CBS, Tony Romo part ways Browns outlast Steelers Duren, Pistons reach deal Story by Wildcats Wire Kentucky at South Carolina: Final Thoughts and Prediction Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Fri, October 2, 2026 at 5:31 PM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kentucky Wildcats have to go on their second road trip of the season as the will face off against South Carolina at 4:15 P.M. ET on Saturday. We have previewed both South Carolina offense and defense, as well as laying out Kentucky's path to victory in this game. This is a massive game for both teams; Kentucky is trying to snap a four game losing streak against the Gamecocks and South Carolina is a desperate trying to turnaround their season. In this article, I will give my final thoughts on the game and a prediction. Kentucky has to win early downs in this game, and they have consistently done that all season on both sides of the football. Kentucky's offense has stayed ahead of schedule consistently and haven't needed to rely on converting third downs, which has been a weak spot for this offense. Kentucky's offensive line has improved every week and they have to dominate the line of scrimmage in this game. They have been phenomenal in run blocking as they lead the country in yards before contact per rush attempt, and they should keep Kenny Minchey clean as South Carolina is without their game-wrecking edge defender Dylan Stewart. Defensively, Kentucky has performed similarly as the offense. They are struggling on third downs, but they have been exceptional on early downs. If they can slow down this South Carolina run game and keep their offense off schedule, it should bode well for the Wildcats defense. Kentucky will probably have a similar defensive gameplan that they had against Texas A&M, contain LaNorris Sellers on the ground and force him to beat you with his arm. Sellers has struggled this season, he has turned the ball over four times. The turnover margin has been the downfall of Kentucky in this series as of late, as the Wildcats have 14 total turnovers in the last five matchups against the Gamecocks. That could flip on Saturday, Kentucky is +3 in the turnover margin on the season, whereas South Carolina is -4 in the turnover margin. Kentucky has done a great job at taking care of the football and creating turnovers on defense. South Carolina has their backs against the wall, head coach Shane Beamer is on a scorching hot seat. They have struggled against SEC opponents and the talk surrounding their program has been extremely loud this week. Combine that with your best player serving a suspension, it will be a lot to overcome for the Gamecocks. Who gets off to a hot start could be the determining factor in this football game. Speaking of hot starts, there are multiple reasons it could play a factor in this game. South Carolina needs to create that early momentum to keep the crowd involved. If Kentucky gets off to a hot start and the Gamecocks struggle offensively, you could see the boo birds come out in Columbia from this fan base. It is worth noting, Kentucky ranks third in the SEC this season in time trailing this season, as the Wildcats have only spent a total of over 26 minutes trailing through the first month of play. Kentucky has been good at getting off to quick starts this season, and I could see that continue on Saturday. Kentucky has a unique offensive scheme that will force a struggling South Carolina defense to communicate. Over the last five meetings, the Wildcats have averaged just 13 points per game, which is the main reason they have been 1-4 over that stretch. I believe Kentucky gets the offense going and South Carolina fails to overcome all the noise surrounding the team this week. Prediction: Kentucky 34, South Carolina 24 This article originally appeared on UK Wildcats Wire: Kentucky at South Carolina: Final Thoughts and Prediction

picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for When the South Carolina Gamecocks Take on Kentucky - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus 49ers owner suspended, fined WNBA playoffs CBS, Tony Romo part ways Browns outlast Steelers Duren, Pistons reach deal Three Bold Predictions for When the South Carolina Gamecocks Take on Kentucky Sep 26, 2026; Tuscaloosa, Alabama, USA; South Carolina Gamecocks quarterback LaNorris Sellers (16) calls for the snap during the first quarter against the Alabama Crimson Tide at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Alex Joyce Fri, October 2, 2026 at 6:17 PM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Despite all the troubles from the last two weeks, South Carolina has a chance to get the train back on the track against Kentucky. For a team desparately needing a win, here are three bold predicitions for the Gamecocks that will ultimately end their 2-game skid this season. Usually we try to give you at least one on each side of the ball, however this week we're changing things up. This is an all offense version of bold predictions. We will focus on LaNorris Sellers, the passing game, and the tailbacks. Passing Game looks smooth again It certainly won't be easy. Though Knetucky's "stats" place them in the bottom half of SEC defenses in the passing category, it doesn't tell the full story. In two SEC games the Wildcats held Alabama's Keelon Russell to 188 yards passing and Texas A&M's Marcel Reed to 236 yards. They also lead the conference in interceptions with 6. What gives me confidence in this specific matchup will be South Carolina's ability to run the ball (more on that later). A good run game can open passing windows for an offense that has struggled in that department for the last two weeks. I expect this to be the case and for Gamecocks to see a better attack than they have in recent weeks. Sep 19, 2026; Columbia, South Carolina, USA; South Carolina Gamecocks wide receiver Mazeo Bennett Jr. (3) attempts to get around Mississippi State Bulldogs safety Isaac Smith (2) in the second quarter at Williams-Brice Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Blake-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect LaNorris Sellers finishes with no interceptions In the last three games, Sellers has four interceptions , two of which came against Mississippi State. On the other side, Kentucky has been great this season at creating turnovers. On paper this is a matchup that favors the Wildcats. However I believe Seller ends his interception streak this week and keeps this passing game on track. Gamecocks rush for 200+ In their two SEC games this season, Kentucky gave up 155 yards and three touchdowns to Bama. Against Texas A&M they gave up 187 yards and two touchdowns. This is a front seven that can be run on and that's exactly what this Gamecocks' offense does best. Matt Fuller leads a rushing attack that is ranked first in the conference with 262 yards per game. Fuller gained 112 yards on the ground last week as the team put up 216 yards total on Alabama. Against Mississippi State running backs totaled 149 yards. That's good enough for 182.5 yards per game through two contests. Fuller should have his third 100 yard rushing performance of the season which will propel the Gamecocks to a win. While the hype and excitement are there, the Wildcats have a big-time game on Saturday on the road against the South Carolina Gamecocks. Fans in Columbia are starting to get really frustrated with the way this team is playing, and some feel that the end could be near for Shane Beamer. The Gamecocks have a very good quarterback in LaNorris Sellers, who has given Kentucky issues during his time in Columbia. away.blurb: South Carolina will have a lot of pressure on them Saturday, while Kentucky wants to get one step closer to bowl game eligibility. With the matchup on the horizon, the injury report was released on Wednesday night. How are things looking? As Will Stein noted on Tuesday, Kentucky has a couple of guys currently questionable, but DJ Miller has popped up as 'Doubtful', who Stein has said has been dealing with a soft tissue, which bothered the sophomore against South Alabama. "There'll be some guys that are questionable for this weekend," Stein said when asked about injuries on Tuesday. "Nothing I would say is season ending or that's going to be more than a game. But I'm expecting to be almost at full health (against South Carolina). ...Hopefully by Saturday, we're up to as full strength as we can be." away.headline: Georgia Southern turns to Sun Belt play after three straight losses
away.blurb: Your Privacy Choices/(Opt-Out of Sale/Targeted Ads) Eagles open conference play at Coastal Carolina with a 1-3 record, plus key injury updates following Saturday’s loss to No. 25 Houston. Georgia Southern is ready to turn the page. The Eagles enter Sun Belt play at 1-3 after dropping three straight games, including Saturday’s 42-28 loss to No. 25 Houston at Allen E. Paulson Stadium. Despite the loss, Georgia Southern showed some encouraging signs offensively. Quarterback Max Johnson turned in his strongest performance of the season, completing 26 of 38 passes for 284 yards and a season-high three touchdowns without an interception. The Eagles also continued to expand the role of quarterback Weston Bryan. Georgia Southern used packages featuring both quarterbacks on the field together, including a flea-flicker that started with Bryan and ended with Johnson finding Alex Taylor for a 40-yard touchdown. Taylor finished with a season-high 119 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Georgia Southern now turns its attention to conference play while also dealing with several injuries. Head coach Clay Helton confirmed Monday that wide receiver Ashton Hollins will undergo season-ending shoulder surgery. Hollins, an Illinois transfer, suffered the injury in the Eagles’ loss at Jacksonville State. Inside linebacker Rashon Myles Jr. also left Saturday’s game against Houston with an Achilles injury. Helton said Myles was scheduled to undergo imaging Monday to determine the extent of the injury. The Eagles were also without two starting offensive tackles against Houston because of illness. Helton said neither had been medically cleared to play. Georgia Southern will now look to regroup as the Sun Belt portion of its schedule begins. The Eagles have lost three straight, while Coastal Carolina enters the matchup at 1-3 and riding a two-game losing streak. Both teams now look for a fresh start, 0-0 in conference play. Saturday will also mark Georgia Southern’s first matchup against the Chanticleers under first-year Coastal Carolina head coach Ryan Beard. The Eagles have won three straight games in the series, including a 26-6 victory in their last trip to Conway in 2024. Georgia Southern leads the all-time series 8-4. Georgia Southern and Coastal Carolina kick off Saturday, Oct. 3, at 7 p.m. from Brooks Stadium in Conway, South Carolina. Miami enters 4-0 and 2-0 in the ACC, while Clemson sits at 3-1 and 2-0 in conference play. The Tigers have won three straight since getting embarrassed 51-10 by LSU in the opener, including a 24-10 road win over Cal last week. But Clemson hasn't faced anything quite like this Miami team since that LSU disaster. The Hurricanes are averaging 51.8 points and 588.8 yards per game , ranking first nationally in total offense. Even scarier, Miami's defense is allowing only 9.0 points and 224.5 yards per game . How Miami Wins It starts with Darian Mensah . Mensah has been ridiculously efficient this season. He completed 23 of 27 passes for 338 yards and three touchdowns in Miami's 52-3 win over Central Michigan, pushing his season completion percentage to an absurd 88.7% . Miami needs to let Mensah attack Clemson early and take the crowd out of the game. Malachi Toney gives him an elite weapon on the outside, while the Hurricanes have enough balance on the ground to prevent Clemson from simply sitting back against the pass. Defensively, the formula is simple: make Clemson throw the football. The Tigers are averaging only 156.3 passing yards per game, while Miami enters with the nation's No. 1 rushing defense at just 39.5 yards allowed per game. If Miami shuts down Clemson's rushing attack early, this matchup could become extremely uncomfortable for the Tigers. How Clemson Wins Clemson needs Death Valley to become a factor immediately. The Tigers cannot afford to get into a shootout with Miami. They need long possessions, a strong rushing performance from Gideon Davidson and at least a couple of turnovers from their defense. Davidson is coming off 159 rushing yards and two touchdowns against Cal , and Clemson will likely need another big performance from him to keep Mensah standing on the sideline. If Clemson falls behind by multiple scores and is forced to throw its way back into the game, Miami has a massive advantage. I think Clemson makes this interesting early. It's a Saturday night game in Death Valley, Clemson has won three straight and the Tigers' defense has shown significant improvement since that LSU embarrassment. But Miami is simply playing at a different level right now. Mensah eventually starts finding holes in the Clemson defense, Miami takes away the Tigers' running game and the Hurricanes begin pulling away in the second half. Clemson has improved, but Miami looks like a legitimate College Football Playoff and national championship contender. This is one heck of a spotlight for just his third start. The Tigers have done their best to alleviate pressure on him with their run game, but Miami leads the ACC with 39.5 rushing yards allowed per game. Clemson may give Gideon Davidson carry after carry, but there will be a time when the Tigers need some big passing plays. Reynolds doesn't have to be Superman, but he has to show some growth. Can he? The combination of a still-developing freshman and an offensive line that's been so-so in pass protection plays into Miami's hands, especially with how much pressure the Hurricanes have been getting on quarterbacks. Clemson is still figuring things out with Reynolds, while Miami has a quarterback with no questions. Darian Mensah will look to do what he did last season at Duke and pick Clemson apart. The Tigers have a strong secondary, but it'll be their toughest challenge yet. Even if Mensah has an off day, the Hurricanes have a strong rushing attack that's gained over 120 yards in all four games. Miami is most likely to have a balanced offense, and it also doesn't have a clear weakness on defense. Clemson's rushing defense struggled against LSU and North Carolina, and while it did better against California, the Golden Bears are averaging an ACC-worst 101.5 rushing yards per game. Ashton Hampton leads the ACC with five pass breakups, and Elliot Washington II is tied for second with three interceptions. Getting Corian Gipson back at nickel would only strengthen an already sound unit. Clemson's secondary will have its hands full though. Mensah has been the nation's most efficient and accurate quarterbacks. But the Tigers are well-equipped to meet the challenge, just like they did against Cal's Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele . Miami ranks second in the ACC with 227.5 rushing yards per game, and running backs Javian Mallory and Mark Fletcher Jr. are averaging 9 and 6.5 yards per carry, respectively. Miami also looks better on the other side. Marquise Lightfoot is tied for fourth in the ACC with four sacks, while Damon Wilson II and Armondo Blount can win one-on-one. But Clemson has been playing much better over the last few weeks, winning three straight games in the process. After a poor showing to open the year against LSU, the Tigers have bounced back fully, with the defense playing much better. Over the last three games, Clemson is only allowing 12.3 points per game, a far cry from the 51-point debacle that happened in Week 1. picks.headline: Miami vs. Clemson final score predictions: Will the Hurricanes continue their dominant start, or can the Tigers pull their season out of the fire?
picks.blurb: Miami vs. Clemson final score predictions: Will the Hurricanes continue their dominant start, or can the Tigers pull their season out of the fire? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus 49ers owner suspended, fined WNBA playoffs CBS, Tony Romo part ways Browns outlast Steelers Duren, Pistons reach deal Sam Navarro-Imagn Images; Ken Ruinard-Imagn Images Craig Smith, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness Thu, October 1, 2026 at 2:23 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Canes and Tigers will have the eyes of the nation on them on Saturday night in a big game for two programs going in different directions. The Miami Hurricanes and Clemson Tigers square off on Saturday night in Death Valley in a game with significant ACC title implications, with the game being shown in primetime on ABC. The Canes have surged to a 4-0 start, with only a slight flutter in the second half at Wake Forest after leading 31-7 being their only show of mortality thus far. Meanwhile, Clemson has improved to 3-1 after a season-opening 51-10 loss at LSU. Lifeless performances against Georgia Southern and in the first half against UNC have turned into a come from behind win over the Tar Heels and an impressive 24-10 win at Cal last weekend. Can the Tigers ride that modest improvement into an upset win on Saturday night? Our college football writers weighed in with their game predictions. Miami 38, Clemson 28 I think the writing is on the wall for Clemson and Dabo Swinney. The program is a shell of itself, esepcially from a talent acquisition standpoint. Things are the exact opposite for the Hurricanes, as they were less than 70 yards away from a national championship. Even so, I expect Clemson to show out for this game almost as a last ditch effort to save their season. It won't be enough, as the Hurricanes prove to be too explosive for the Tigers. Tyler Forness , A to Z Sports Florida Miami 30, Clemson 10 This game had the potential to be one of the better matchups in the ACC this season if Clemson held up their end of the bargain, but it looks like Dabo and the boys have only fallen further down the list in terms of program competence. The quarterback position is a mess, and a lot of the notable draft prospects heading into the season simply haven't played up to the offseason hype. On the other hand, you have a Miami team with not only one of the sport's most explosive weapons in Malachi Toney, but also one of the most efficient passers in college football in Darian Mensah. I know Clemson is at home, but this has a chance to be a route for the Hurricanes. Give me Miami, big. Rob Gregson , A to Z Sports Alabama Miami 34, Clemson 21 This game is much closer than the final score suggests, with Clemson hanging around for a large portion of the afternoon. One of the biggest storylines will be how the Tigers handle Malachi Toney. It'll be interesting to see if Clemson allows CB Ashton Hampton to follow Toney around the field and essentially shadow him, considering Hampton is the most talented defensive back Miami has faced to this point. If Clemson can limit Toney and force Miami to win elsewhere, the Tigers have a chance to make this uncomfortable. Ultimately, though, Miami's overall talent takes over as the game progresses. The Hurricanes make enough explosive plays on offense to create separation, while Clemson capitalizes on a couple of coverage busts from the Miami secondary for some big plays of its own. Miami's depth and playmakers prove to be the difference in the second half, allowing the Hurricanes to pull away and finish with a 34-21 victory. Ryan Roberts , A to Z Sports Notre Dame Miami 30, Clemson 13 This feels like a game that could be closer than many pundits are giving it credit for, and perhaps those in Las Vegas as well. The 17-point line feels out of place for what Clemson has been over the last decade, but Dabo Swinney's Tigers have looked anything but the part of contenders the last few years. Clemson's secondary is talented, led by Ashton Hampton, who could play himself into first round consideration in April's NFL Draft. I could see the Tigers giving Miami's offense problems and preventing some of the chunk plays that Miami has ripped off all year with the exception of a quarter and a half against Wake Forest. But Clemson freshman QB Tait Reynolds is going to have a rough experience against a Miami team that's starting to get a tad healthier on the defensive side of the ball. DL Ahmad Moten, Sr. and Armondo Blount are off the injury report and appear set to be available on Saturday, along with CB Damari Brown. Starting CB Xavier Lucas could even possibly be in play, but even if not, Ethan O'Connor has been one of the better CBs in the ACC this year and can handle things very capably. Miami slowly puts this one away in the second half with Mark Fletcher, Jr., who is also off the injury report, pounding away in the fourth quarter on a tired defense. away.headline: Why the No. 4 Miami Hurricanes Should Limit Starters Returning From Injury
away.blurb: MIAMI, Fla. – After missing last Saturday's 52-3 win over Central Michigan at Hard Rock Stadium, the No. 4 Miami Hurricanes are set for the return of running back Mark Fletcher Jr. and defensive tackle Ahmad Moten Sr. (both seniors) against Clemson , but it should be taken with caution. The backfield supporting cast suffered a difficult loss of redshirt junior CharMar "Marty" Brown, who is out for the rest of the season with a severe right knee injury, which was sustained against Wake Forest on Sept. 18. He was the primary backup to Fletcher Jr., but an opportunity for more snaps presents itself. For starters, Fletcher Jr. shouldn't return to a heavy workload. As the Hurricanes' go-to running back, the 21-year-old's long-term availability is valuable. Fletcher Jr. proved to turn things up a notch when the lights got brighter in last year's historic run to the National Championship game. Plus, Pringle Jr., Mallory, and Wheatley-Humphrey can gain experience playing college football in a hostile environment. Memorial Stadium, otherwise known as Death Valley, is one of the sport's most historic venues. Pringle Jr. only logged six snaps in last year's College Football Playoffs and Wheatley-Humphrey had 19, but only on special teams. As Hurricanes offensive coordinator Shannon Dawson looks to spread the workload in the backfield, this Saturday presents an opportunity to play at least four different running backs. They will be facing Clemson 's junior linebacker, Sammy Brown , who was the ACC Defensive Rookie of the Year in 2024. Moten Sr. is off to a slow start this season. Thus far, in 91 snaps across three games, he's logged three total tackles, a solo and two assists, 0.5 tackles for loss, 0.5 sacks, and four pressures. Moten Sr. suffered a left shoulder injury against Wake Forest, left early, then returned to play the rest of the game. Despite having first-round projections in the 2027 NFL Draft, the Hurricanes still need the star defender healthy in the long run. It presents an opportunity for sophomore Jarquez Carter and junior Keona Davis, who have been serviceable in reserve roles, to step up. home.headline: Dabo Swinney provides update on Christopher Vizzina injury, Clemson backup QB plan
home.blurb: Clemson quarterback Christopher Vizzina (right) injured his left elbow against Georgia Southern, but coach Dabo Swinney (left) said Vizzina will still be available vs. North Carolina. Clemson QB Christopher Vizzina is available, coach Dabo Swinney said, but not 100 percent recovered from a small fracture in his left elbow. What’s the Tigers’ plan if they need a backup to play vs. Miami? Clemson listed Vizzina as a game-time decision in the final availability report before Clemson’s Sept. 19 win over North Carolina. He was left off the final report entirely before the Sept. 25 win at Cal. He was listed as Clemson’s backup quarterback on the depth chart vs. Miami, per team release. Top Story Dabo Swinney provides update on Christopher Vizzina injury, Clemson backup QB plan By Jackson Castellano jcastellano@postandcourier.com Jackson Castellano Tigers coach Dabo Swinney said Vizzina is throwing and practicing after sustaining a small left elbow fracture Sept. 12 against Georgia Southern. However, Swinney said that Trent Pearman would be Clemson’s second option at quarterback vs. Miami if necessary. “He's still not 100 percent on his left arm, so if he plays, he plays with a brace on it to protect it,” Swinney said. “But it's really more just the range of motion for him, kind of getting that back fully. But it's gotten a little better each day.” Swinney said Vizzina could play in an emergency. He wasn’t listed in the initial ACC availability report Sept. 30. The senior has 14 completions for 102 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions this season. He was in the running for Clemson’s QB1 job with freshman Tait Reynolds during preseason camp, but Vizzina was ultimately named the starter in Week 1. Vizzina played three drives in the 22-7 win over Georgia Southern before Reynolds took over. The pair had previously split reps in a 51-10 loss to LSU. Reynolds was named the starter moving forward after the Georgia Southern game, but Swinney said the change had nothing to do with Vizzina’s health. In two career starts and four total games, Reynolds has thrown for 521 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. Pearman, a fifth-year senior , joined Clemson as a walk-on in 2022. He has 10 passing attempts in his career, completing four for 43 yards. The D.W. Daniel graduate has played 33 career snaps. Reynolds will start for Clemson (3-1, 2-0 ACC) in its Oct. 3 matchup with No. 4 Miami (4-0, 2-0). Reach Jackson Castellano at jcastellano@po

Miami has been playing without three of its top cornerbacks basically all season, with starters Lucas and OJ Frederique out since the Stanford game and sophomore reserve Ja'Boree Antoine out since before the season began. Other players who sat out or were banged up against Central Michigan but don't appear on the availability report: running back Mark Fletcher Jr. , defensive linemen Ahmad Moten Sr. and Armondo Blount, and linebacker Kellen Wiley. Linebacker Ezekiel Marcelin is listed as questionable and reserve tight end Owen Ruskavich is out. As for Clemson, two players are listed as questionable (defensive end Armon Mason and Elyjah Thurmon), while seven have been ruled out (safety Polo Anderson, cornerback Shavar Young Jr., wide receiver Cole Turner , running back David Eziomume, defensive tackles Kourtney Kelly and Markus Strong, and offensive lineman Mason Wade). Hurricanes coach Mario Cristobal on Monday said Lucas was "getting closer" to returning to game action. "Not all the way there yet," Cristobal said. "Hopefully, good news later this week. There's been a lot of progress. Works his butt off, but not all the way there." In their absence, the trio of Ethan O'Connor, Damari Brown and safety Bryce Fitzgerald have been Miami's primary outside cornerbacks. Speaking of Brown, he did not play last week against Central Michigan but does not have an injury designation, signaling that he should be good to go against Clemson.
